Summary: Phase 1 render service (Puppeteer image render)
Description: Spin up a render endpoint that takes { mediaId, template, aspectRatio, format } and returns a rendered PNG. Uses Puppeteer to load a stripped-down /render.html page that reuses the preview render code at exact pixel dimensions, screenshots, uploads to Cloudinary, persists RenderArtifact. Image-only for Phase 1; video comes in Phase 2.

Summary: Inline Render button on each Creative Template Preview card
Description: Add a Render PNG action next to the validation status on each preview card in the Creative Template Preview panel. On click: POST /api/render, show spinner, display thumbnail + download link when done.

Summary: Rendered Creatives gallery panel
Description: New section below Creative Template Preview showing all RenderArtifacts for the current Media. Each card: template name, aspect ratio, format, thumbnail, file size, Open / Download / Push-to-campaign actions. Includes a Render all button that queues every template-ratio combo that passes validation.

Summary: Batch render on rights approval
Description: When rights.approved flips to true, enqueue render jobs for the top N viable (template, ratio) combinations so creatives are pre-warmed for campaign push.

Summary: Phase 2 render service: separate deployment + video rendering
Description: Split the render service into its own Render deployment with a Puppeteer worker pool. Add ffmpeg-based video pipeline for MP4 output; compose source video clips with overlays via CSS animation captured as frames. Migrate off in-process deployment.

Summary: Video overlay zones: pass cross-frame safeRect as forbidden to Gemini
Description: The detect pipeline already computes safeRect (union of all YOLO detections across frames + primary subjects). Thread it into the overlay-zone Gemini prompt as an explicit forbidden rect so creator-subject motion doesn't collide with overlays in the clip.

Summary: Video overlay zones: multi-frame analysis (sample 3 frames)
Description: For video Media, sample start/middle/end frames of the clip, run overlay-zone analysis on each, union the forbidden rects and intersect the safe zones. Replaces the current hero-frame-only analysis.

Summary: Video overlay zones: analyze rendered self-underlay output
Description: Extract N frames from the rendered self-underlay Cloudinary video URL via so_<sec> transforms and analyze those instead of the hero frame. Highest fidelity, highest cost; only do this once real overlay-on-video failures surface.

Summary: Populate media.supporting_media with secondary smart-crop winner
Description: Currently null; slot chain falls through to product.hero_media so results_proof shows the same image twice. Pick an alternate-ratio smart-crop winner as media.supporting_media[0] so the support_media zone renders a complementary framing.

Summary: Populate media.background_media as source fallback
Description: Populate media.background_media with the source fileUrl so templates that reach the end of the support_media source_priority chain have a blurred-bg fallback asset.

Summary: Add overlay-mode variants for other templates
Description: Roll out the image-as-canvas placement pattern to ugc_split_screen, review_collage, results_proof, creator_endorsement — register each as <template>_overlay with its own priority + region hints. Validate against real media.

Summary: Iterate overlay placement quality from real-world renders
Description: Review placement outputs across brands/ratios, tune region hints, size bounds, scrim strength, inset fallback thresholds based on visual quality feedback.

Summary: Add 16:9 aspect ratio to extendedCropsService
Description: The renderer's canvas spec supports 16:9 but extendedCropsService only produces 9:16 and 1.91:1. Add 16:9 entry to NEW_RATIOS so horizontal placements get AI-extended assets instead of falling back to a base-ratio winner.

Summary: Judge bias fix: defects-list pass before scoring
Description: The current extended-crop judge has residual self-preference bias for gpt-image-1 over Gemini that slot-blinding + weighting + tighter rejects didn't fully address. Change the prompt to require an itemized per-candidate defects list before scoring. Forces detection of label / shape / text mutations a holistic score glosses over.

Summary: Judge bias fix: cross-provider second opinion
Description: Run Gemini 2.5 Pro as a second judge in parallel with the GPT-4.1 judge; only declare a winner when both models agree. On disagreement, fall back to the label_logo_fidelity leader. Structurally eliminates self-preference.

Summary: Judge bias fix: OCR verification of source text
Description: We already detect source text in subjectTextService. Run OCR on each extended-crop candidate and auto-reject any that's missing a detected source token. Objective tie-break.

Summary: Upload YOLO primary product crop for tightest Lens match
Description: For video Media, upload the YOLO primary product cropBuffer as a separate Cloudinary image and pass its URL to Lens. Tightest possible match isolation.

Summary: Brand curation UI (list + edit)
Description: Simple admin screen at /brands that lists all Brand docs (stub / enriched / curated), supports edit of name, tagline, logo, colors, font, demographics. Flips source=curated so automatic enrichment never overwrites. Needed once stub-only brands are obviously wrong.

Summary: Persona avatar generation via gpt-image-1
Description: Generate an avatarUrl per demographic in Brand.demographics[] by calling gpt-image-1 with the persona description. Uploads to Cloudinary, sets demographic.avatarUrl. Used by the renderer for quote attribution avatars in creator_endorsement / review_collage.

Summary: Brand font loading in preview + renderer
Description: When brand.font_family is set, load the font from Google Fonts or a bundled WOFF/WOFF2 in the preview page and the Puppeteer render context. Currently we just set the CSS font-family and hope the viewer has it installed.

Summary: BrandCanvasVariant promotion flow from AI Layout Studio
Description: If AI Layout Studio outputs prove viable, add a Use this layout button on each extracted reference that promotes it to a BrandCanvasVariant document (brandId, variantName, aspectRatio, canvasSpec). Template picker surfaces these alongside the 5 canonical templates.

Summary: Webhook ingestion for Meta / TikTok / Instagram
Description: Receive posts via webhook, upsert Media by (source, externalId), populate metadata.{creatorName, creatorHandle, caption, postedAt, hashtags}, platformStats.{views, likes, comments, shares, saves}, rights state. Enqueue DetectRun automatically. Unblocks real engagement data for performance.metrics and performance.engagement.

Summary: adSuitability scoring writer
Description: Compute Media.adSuitability { score, reasons, updatedAt } after a DetectRun completes. Heuristic over product count, primary-subject quality, judge scores, engagement density, review signal. Powers a Find ad-suitable media query for future ad-layout service batches.

Summary: Dedicated rights management screen
Description: Standalone screen listing all Media with pending / approved / revoked rights, batch approval, audit of approvedBy / approvedAt / notes. Current inline toggle on detect review page is adequate for single-media flow but won't scale once webhook ingestion feeds many media at once.

Summary: Product records with source lineage on approval
Description: When an operator approves a YOLO product card into inventory, the resulting Product doc should carry sourceMediaId, sourceRunId, sourceYoloProductId so we can audit where it came from and re-run with the original media if needed.

Summary: Migrate legacy inventory pipeline to Run-style entity
Description: The truck-photo upload and pre-cropped bridge still use the legacy Job model. Move to a PrecroppedRun / InventoryRun lifecycle consistent with DetectRun so both paths share the split-service architecture pattern.

Summary: Consume overlay restrictions + brightnessGrid in renderer
Description: The renderer v1 doc references scrim application rules but doesn't reference our per-image restrictions[] / brightnessGrid. Wire the overlay-zone analysis into the renderer so scrim placement and hard keep-outs are driven by real image data rather than hardcoded heuristics.

Summary: Expose judge primaryId as the single source of truth
Description: resolvePrimarySubjectDesc already prefers judge.subjects.primaryId. Audit all other consumers of subjects (extended crops prompts, match service, overlay zones) to make sure none of them silently fall back to GPT's role assignment when a judge pick exists. Document the precedence rule in the subject-text service header.

Summary: Inset-mode band crowding: CTA fails to place after headline consumes full band
Description: In inset mode, higher-priority elements (logo, headline, product_meta) consume the full width of a narrow band, leaving no room for the CTA. Candidate generator in inset path emits left/centered/right anchors per shape but not anchors that sit RIGHT-OF-CONSUMED. Smoke test: 9:16 portrait with centered-person subject reliably reproduces. Fix: sub-divide bands by consumed rects between elements, or add a right-of-consumed anchor, or shrink earlier elements more aggressively when a required later element would otherwise fail.

Summary: Enforce canvas safe-margin in placement
Description: Today candidate generation uses scattered 0.04/0.05/0.95/0.96 literals so effective safe margins drift between 2%-5% depending on region (bottom-third anchor at y=0.90 + shape h=0.08 lands y2=0.98 = 2% from edge). Step 1: introduce SAFE_MARGIN const (0.05) and withinSafeArea helper; replace the scattered literals. Step 2 (later): per-edge margins keyed on platform (Meta/TikTok/IG reserve different HUD/caption zones).

Summary: Wire orphan canonical fields into templates
Description: Audit found ~15 canonical input fields that are derived but never rendered: theme.{style,background_style,emphasis}, layout_options.*, copy.{highlight_text,disclaimer}, cta.{subtext,offer_text}, product.{description,short_benefits,category,currency,id}, trust.{retailer_logos,certifications,press_mentions}, performance.engagement.{shares,saves,views}, ugc.{post_id,post_type,shares,saves,rights_approved}, creator.avatar. Decide per-field: kill, expose in canonical templates, or wire into overlay-mode renderer. Especially high-leverage: theme block (could drive emphasis-based priority reshuffling, style overrides, background treatments, variant generation) and copy.eyebrow (small kicker above overlay headline).

Summary: Hybrid art-director: LLM theme/treatment decisions, heuristic placement execution
Description: Use one Gemini Vision call per Media to emit high-level art direction (theme.emphasis, theme.style, theme.background_style, per-element treatment hints) — then heuristic placement engine executes those decisions across every (template, aspect_ratio) combo. Trades off pure-LLM placement (slow, costly, non-deterministic, weak coordinate math, no measure-and-shrink) for LLM aesthetic judgment + heuristic exactness. Cost collapses from O(templates × ratios) to O(1) calls/Media; outputs stay deterministic and debuggable; brand voice stays consistent across ratios. Implementation order: (1) emit theme block during layout-input assembly, (2) wire theme.emphasis to placement-priority shuffle, (3) wire theme.style to typography overrides table, (4) wire theme.background_style to Cloudinary bg treatment.

Summary: detect.html: live-react to brand-picker change
Description: ads.html listens for window brand:change and reloads its media library. detect.html does not — page-load picks up the new X-Brand-Id but a brand switch while on detect leaves stale data visible. Add a brand:change listener that clears state + redraws.

Summary: detect upload form: drop redundant Brand-name field
Description: With the nav brand picker active, the brand the user is uploading for is implicit (X-Brand-Id header). The Brand input on the upload form is now duplicate context and a source of confusion (what if user types a different brand than the one selected?). Replace the input with a small Active brand: <name> indicator + a Change link that opens the picker.

Summary: Brand management UI (rename / archive / delete)
Description: Today brands are immutable from the UI — only created via the picker. Need a settings page or modal to: rename a brand, archive (soft-delete with status), permanently delete (with confirmation + media cascade rules). Also: edit websiteUrl, primaryColor, custom logoUrl, tone[], demographics. Today the catalog mutates only via auto-enrichment + curatedFields lock; this surfaces those fields directly.

Summary: Tenancy phase 4: team invitations + multi-Advertiser membership
Description: Add AdvertiserMembership join collection so a user can belong to multiple Advertisers (agency model). Invitation flow: an admin emails an invite link with a signed token, the invitee accepts to join the Advertiser as editor/viewer. requireAuth gains an active-Advertiser concept (header X-Advertiser-Id similar to X-Brand-Id) and falls back to the users sole membership when not specified.

Summary: IG V2: CLIP visual matching of YOLO crops against catalog images
Description: Generate CLIP embeddings on catalog Product images at ingest, store as Float32 vector on Product. Match service: encode each YOLO crop and rank catalog Products by cosine similarity. Catalog visual hits with cosine > threshold supplement (or replace) text+category matching. This is the real unlock for "model wearing what we sell" matches where text overlap is weak (a generic "tee shirt" YOLO label binds to the right SKU because its visual signature matches one catalog item).

Summary: IG V2: scheduled auto-sync with per-brand daily DetectRun cap
Description: Cron job pulls catalog daily and IG posts hourly per connected Brand. Cap auto-DetectRuns at N posts/day per brand to control compute spend. Manual sync buttons remain. Add brand-level setting for cadence + cap. Skip already-ingested externalIds via the upsert key.

Summary: IG V2: catalog browser panel on brand.html
Description: Paginated grid of Product rows under each Brand: image thumbnail, title, price, productUrl, last-seen-in-match count. Filters by category, in-stock, has-reviews. "Refresh reviews" button per Product. Lets ops eyeball whether catalog sync produced sensible data and which SKUs are seeing match traffic.

Summary: IG V2: media-source indicator on detect.html
Description: Distinguish uploaded vs IG-sourced Media in the inventory list and detect view. Small pill: "Manual upload" / "Instagram post" / "Instagram reel". For IG-sourced, surface the original IG URL, posted date, and creator handle as read-only metadata.

Summary: IG V2: multi-page-per-brand + Reels-specific frame extraction
Description: Allow more than one IG account per Brand (e.g. main brand page + creator collabs). Reels need per-frame YOLO + audio Whisper transcription; static posts skip transcription. Auto-detect media type from Graph API media_type field and route to the right pipeline shape.

Summary: IG V3: Meta webhooks for real-time post ingest
Description: Subscribe to Meta page-feed webhooks. New post events trigger immediate ingest + DetectRun (subject to daily cap). Requires Meta app review for webhook subscriptions in production. Eliminates polling latency.

Summary: IG V3: cross-brand catalog dedup
Description: Same SKU sold under multiple Advertiser accounts (agencies, parent/child brands) creates duplicate Product rows. Add an optional canonicalProductId pointer or a (gtin, brandFamily) dedup index. Reviews + match-history can then be shared across the duplicates.

Summary: IG V3: auto-suggest product matches in IG comments
Description: When a post triggers a confident product_match outcome, optionally post a reply comment on the original IG post linking to the matched product page. Requires explicit per-Brand opt-in and rate limiting. Closes the loop from social signal to commerce conversion.

Summary: Catalog browser: surface review quotes when hasReviews=true
Description: The /api/integrations/instagram/catalog list endpoint returns hasReviews, reviewsRating, and reviewsCount but omits the actual quotes blob to keep paginated responses light. Decide between two surfacings: (a) return productReviews inline in the list response when hasReviews=true (heavier payload), or (b) add an expand-on-click flow in the card that fetches GET /catalog/:id/reviews on demand. Recommend (b) — keeps the grid fast and lets the card animate in 4-6 quotes inline. Either way the card should show at least one teaser quote without a round-trip.

Summary: Ad platforms: end-to-end OAuth + scope validation
Description: Cap off Ad Platforms Phase A by validating both Meta Ads and Google Ads OAuth flows against real ad accounts. Punchlist: (1) Meta App — request Advanced Access on ads_read / ads_management / business_management via App Review (Standard Access works for the app's own admin/dev/tester roles, blocks public users); (2) Meta App — confirm both /instagram/callback and /meta-ads/callback are registered as Valid OAuth Redirect URIs; (3) Google Cloud — get the OAuth consent screen verified for the sensitive adwords scope, or list our admin emails as Test users while in Testing publishing status; (4) Google Ads API Center — confirm developer token has Standard or Basic Access (not just Test); (5) e2e walk: connect each platform from the brand page, finalize via picker, sync campaigns once, verify Campaign rows land with productSetIds populated. Tracks the lingering Meta OAuth perms questions + the Google v17 sunset that surfaced during testing.

Summary: Upload Consolidation + Detect→Catalog Auto-create
Description: One unified Upload tab replacing the legacy /inventory and /detect pages. Top-level type picker (Product or Social Post/Reel) routes to the appropriate pipeline — minimal Cloudinary+CatalogProduct path for products, full detect pipeline for media. Closes the loop with auto-creation of draft CatalogProduct rows from confident product_match outcomes when the brand has opted in. Stories below cover schema, UI consolidation, the two upload endpoints, auto-create wiring, draft management, and the per-brand toggle. Stories 2–7 can land in parallel after Story 1 ships the schema additions.

Summary: Upload-1: Schema additions (CatalogProduct.source draft / detectedFromMediaId + Brand.uploadSettings.autoCreateFromDetect)
Description: Foundation. CatalogProduct.source enum gains 'detect-identified'. CatalogProduct adds draft: Boolean (default false) — flags rows missing commerce-required fields (price, productUrl) so the catalog browser can surface them as a separate completion queue. CatalogProduct adds detectedFromMediaId: ObjectId ref Media (back-pointer for audit + quick navigation). Brand schema adds uploadSettings { autoCreateFromDetect: Boolean (default false) } controlling whether confident matches auto-write drafts. Indexes: (brandId, draft) for the draft-filter query.

Summary: Upload-2: Unified Upload page (replace /inventory + /detect entry points)
Description: One /upload route with a type picker at top (Product | Social Post / Reel). Selecting a type swaps the form below. Reuses existing /detect.html flow for media (full results view stays where it is) and a new minimal product-form below. Old /inventory + /detect URLs redirect to /upload (or stay live as deep-links pointing at the right tab). Nav simplifies to one Upload entry alongside Detection Review, Ad Generation, Brand, Members.

Summary: Upload-3: Product upload endpoint + form
Description: POST /api/upload/product takes { title, price, currency, productUrl, gtin?, mpn?, category?, description?, image (file) }. Server uploads image to Cloudinary, optionally background-removes (V2), creates a CatalogProduct row with source='manual-upload' (new enum value) under the active brand. Returns the created row. Form on the unified Upload page has the required fields + drag-drop image. Manual products show in the catalog browser alongside ig-catalog rows but are tagged as Manual.

Summary: Upload-4: Auto-create draft CatalogProduct from confident detect matches
Description: After productMatchService produces a product_match outcome where winner !== 'catalog' (no existing match), AND Brand.uploadSettings.autoCreateFromDetect is true, AND identification.certainty >= 0.85, fire-and-forget create a draft CatalogProduct: { source: 'detect-identified', draft: true, externalId: detect:<runId>:<idx>, title, description from primarySubjectDesc, category, imageUrl from the tight smart-crop, brand, brandId, advertiserId, detectedFromMediaId }. Idempotent: dedupe via existing same-run draft check before creating. Pipeline never blocks on this.

Summary: Upload-5: Catalog browser drafts tab + inline completion
Description: Catalog browser gets a Drafts filter (or separate section) showing draft=true rows that need commerce completion. Each draft card has inline edit fields for price + productUrl (the two minimums to flip draft=false). Save clears the draft flag. Optional: GTIN/MPN/availability fields collapsed under an Advanced section. Count badge in the integrations card so the user knows how many drafts are waiting (e.g. "Drafts (12)").

Summary: Upload-6: Per-brand auto-create toggle UI
Description: Brand page integrations area gains a small toggle row: "Auto-add detected products as drafts." Off by default. Tooltip explains: confident detect matches automatically create draft catalog rows that need price + URL filled in before they're usable. Persists via PATCH /api/brand/:id (uploadSettings.autoCreateFromDetect).

Summary: Upload-7: Promote-to-product CTA on detect results view
Description: Even when auto-create is off, give users a manual escape hatch: a small "Save as draft product" button on confident product_match results in detect.html. Click → creates the same draft CatalogProduct shape Upload-4 produces, then surfaces in the catalog browser. Useful for opt-in users who want manual control instead of bulk auto-create.

Summary: Chakra UI Migration — Page Rebuilds
Description: Reach Social redesign. Phases 1-3 (shell + theme + auth/brand context + brand picker) shipped. This epic covers the actual page ports (Phases 4-7) PLUS Phase A — a Media Library page that is a Phase 6 detect-rebuild precursor and the first net-new page in the Chakra app (rather than a port of legacy HTML). Each story rebuilds a vanilla HTML page as a React+Chakra component tree using the shipped PipelineShell + theme + apiFetch + useBrand hooks. Phase 4 (Brand) is the heaviest given current brand.html surface area and is broken into 4a-4d sub-stories. Phase A is the lightest path for ops/smoke-test value and breaks into A-0 (backend derivations: adSuitability score + bullets, mood, scene type, focus, concise primary subject label), A-1 (page core: canvas + sidebar + overlays + aspect strip), A-2 (right-sidebar tabs: AI Summary, Detected Products, Scene & Subjects, Technical Insights, Objects, Crops, Text, Layout, Palette), and A-3 (Collections + per-product evidence drill-in + three-tier review slide-over). Phase A components (MediaList, Canvas, OverlayLayers, AspectRatioStrip) lift-and-shift into Phase 6 when it lands.

Summary: Phase 4a: Brand page core (header + identity form + sticky save + live enrichment)
Description: Port the brand.html identity/visual/voice form sections, the header card (logo + name + source pill + website + Refresh enrichment button + enrichment-stage live status), and the sticky save bar with dirty tracking. PATCH /api/brand/:id wiring via apiFetch. ~3 days.

Summary: Phase 4b: Brand integrations card (IG + Meta Ads + Google Ads + pickers)
Description: Port the integrations card from brand.html: IG row + accounts list + status, Meta Ads + Google Ads rows, plus the three picker modals (V2.5 IG account picker, Meta Ads ad-account picker, Google Ads customer picker). All OAuth bounce handling moves into AuthContext. ~3-4 days.

Summary: Phase 4c: Catalog browser + drafts editor
Description: Port the catalog browser panel: paginated grid, filters (q/category/inStock/hasReviews/draftsOnly), source pills, draft inline editor, refresh-reviews per card, totalDrafts badge in header. ~2 days.

Summary: Phase 4d: Brand settings (auto-sync + comment-reply + auto-add-detect + demographics + reviews)
Description: Port the remaining brand.html cards: auto-sync row + cap input, comment-reply row + template editor + cap, auto-add-detect toggle, demographics list (read-only), brand reviews list (read-only). ~2 days.

Summary: Phase 5: Upload page rebuild
Description: Port upload.html — type picker (Product / Social Post) + product form (drag-drop + title + price + currency + URL + GTIN + description) + media form (drag-drop + brand + category + caption). Submits via apiFetch; media submit redirects to /detect?runId=<id>. Reuses Phase 4 design vocabulary. ~3 days.

Summary: Phase 6: Detect page rebuild
Description: Port detect.html results view (no upload form — that's Phase 5's job): summary cards, products + bboxes overlay, subjects + text overlays, smart crops, extended crops, judge results, product matches with identification card + Save-as-draft CTA, overlay zones, transcript+NER (video), AI Layout Studio panel. Largest single page; estimate ~5-7 days.

Summary: Phase 7: Ad Generation page rebuild
Description: Port ads.html — media picker, template preview, brand object inspector, matching tab, validation status, render CTA. Includes the templatePreview.js content. ~4-5 days.

Summary: Detect pipeline: within-run parallelism (Promise.all stage groups)
Description: Today pipelines/detect.js runs stages strictly sequentially even when there are no data dependencies between them. Identify groups that can run in parallel and wrap each group in a single Promise.all. First-pass candidates with verified independence: (a) post-detection enrichment fan-out — subjects-text (GPT-4.1) + product-match providers + transcript NER all read the YOLO output but write to separate artifacts, can run as one Promise.all instead of three serial awaits; (b) smart-crops + extended-crops can start the moment detection completes, in parallel with subjects-text; (c) overlay-zones analysis only needs hero crop + safeRect — can fan out per ratio. Expected 30-50%% speedup per run on top of the WORKER_CONCURRENCY parallelism we already have across runs. Risks: stage timings telemetry needs reworking (currently single-threaded sequential timing), and error handling has to fail the whole run if any parallel branch throws (use Promise.allSettled + collect errors instead of bubble). Worth a careful PR — affects every run.
column9: Currently any Google account can sign in (allowlist removed in 540f01e to unblock dev). Before public launch, add a gate: invite tokens (similar to AdvertiserMembership invitations already shipped), or an email-domain allowlist on Advertiser, or a waitlist flow that holds new signups in a 'pending' status until an admin approves. Whichever we pick, the check goes back into the GoogleStrategy callback in server/index.js where the @floodqrf.com check used to live.

Summary: IG V3 followup: UGC rights-request comment flow
Description: Distinct from V3 #3 (commerce nudges on the brand's own posts). When a creator's post features the brand (discovered via /me/tags or branded-content tags), auto-comment asking for permission to use the content in marketing. Components: (1) discovery — periodically pull tagged-in posts via Graph API endpoint; (2) per-brand opt-in + custom template referencing creator handle and a terms URL; (3) reply parser — when the creator replies with the configured magic word (default "YES"), flip the Media's rights.approved=true and stamp the consent message as audit trail; (4) cap + already-asked idempotency on Media.metadata.rightsRequestAt. Requires the same instagram_manage_comments scope already added in V3 #3 plus instagram_basic for tagged-media reads.

Summary: Ad Platforms Phase B — Campaign read sync
Description: Read campaigns + ad sets/groups + ads from connected Meta and Google Ads accounts. Capture targeting (demo, geo, interests), schedule (start/end), objective, status, budget, and the product set / merchant center IDs each ad references — those product IDs are the join key that lets ads.html filter media-picker results to ones that match the active campaign's products. Read-only in this epic; ship-to-platform (Phase D) is separate. Stories below cover schema + Meta sync + Google sync + scheduler + UI; written so they can be done in parallel after the schema lands.

Summary: Phase B-1: Campaign collection + per-platform sync interface
Description: New Campaign mongoose model { advertiserId, brandId, platform: 'meta-ads'|'google-ads', externalId, name, status, objective, budget, schedule {start,end}, targeting {demo,geo,interests}, productSetIds[], adSets: [{ externalId, name, status, productSetId, ads: [{externalId, name, creativeRef}] }], lastSyncedAt }. Compound unique index (brandId, platform, externalId) for idempotent upsert. Plus a stub services/campaignSyncService.js with the platform-dispatch shape (calls metaAds vs googleAds adapters). Foundation for B-2 / B-3 / B-4.

Summary: Phase B-2: Meta Ads campaign sync adapter
Description: services/metaAdsCampaignService.js. Uses the stored long-lived token + ad-account id from the IntegrationCredential to paginate /act_<id>/campaigns?fields=id,name,status,objective,daily_budget,lifetime_budget,start_time,stop_time,promoted_object,product_set_id then per-campaign /campaign-id/adsets and /adset-id/ads. Maps Meta's targeting spec (geo_locations, age_min, age_max, interests) into the unified Campaign.targeting shape. Idempotent upsert keyed on (brandId, platform='meta-ads', externalId). Captures Meta product_set_id on each ad set so the matcher can filter Media by overlapping CatalogProducts later.

Summary: Phase B-3: Google Ads campaign sync adapter
Description: services/googleAdsCampaignService.js. Uses the stored refresh_token to mint an access token, then the searchStream endpoint with a GAQL query pulling campaign + ad_group + ad + ad_group_criterion + customer_negative_criterion. Pulls Performance Max asset groups + their listing_group_filter (which references Merchant Center product IDs) so Phase C can match those against CatalogProduct. Maps Google's targeting (geo, age, audience criteria) into the unified Campaign.targeting shape. Idempotent upsert keyed on (brandId, platform='google-ads', externalId).

Summary: Phase B-4: Sync routes + manual-trigger UI
Description: REST endpoints under /api/integrations/{meta-ads,google-ads}/sync-campaigns and /campaign-status. Mirror the IG catalog/posts route shape (foreground sync, returns counts + perCredential breakdown). Frontend: "Sync campaigns" button in each Ad Platforms card row plus an ingested-count pill + last-synced timestamp. Read-only for now — campaign list view is Phase B-6.

Summary: Phase B-5: Scheduled auto-sync of campaigns
Description: Extend services/scheduledSyncService.js with a campaigns tier: every Brand.syncSettings.campaignCadenceHours (default 6h) sweep active meta-ads + google-ads credentials and refresh their campaigns. Reuses the existing tick interval; per-credential lastCampaignSyncAt timestamp on IntegrationCredential. Brand-level toggle reuses existing autoSyncEnabled flag — no new opt-in switch needed.

Summary: Phase B-6: Campaign browser panel on brand page
Description: Collapsible card under Ad Platforms (mirrors the V2 #1 catalog browser). Paginated list of Campaigns showing platform pill, name, objective, status, schedule, ad-set count, and product-set overlap with our CatalogProduct collection. Filters by platform / status / objective. Per-row drill-down expands to show ad sets + ads + targeting summary. Read-only — drives the Phase C campaign-aware media filter on ads.html.

Summary: Detect pipeline: declarative stage registry
Description: Refactor pipelines/detect.js so each stage is declared as { name, dependencies, run(ctx) → artifact } and a topological-sort scheduler runs them with Promise.allSettled per dependency level. Replaces the imperative procedural pipeline (still ~700 lines after the within-run-parallelism PR) with a small core that loads stages from a stages/ directory and runs them in dependency order. Goal: adding a new stage becomes 'drop a file in stages/ + declare what it reads', not 'find the right place in detect.js and rewire the call graph by hand'. Aligns with the architecture intent that detect is staged for eventual split into independent services. Builds on the within-run parallelism PR; do this only after that ships and we have real telemetry on which stages benefit most from parallel execution.

Summary: Layout: signal-driven template selector + theme prompt cleanup
Description: Two-part. PART 1 — new services/templateSelectorService.js. Deterministic scorer: loads detection + match + media artifacts for a Media; builds a flat signal sheet (hasReviews, reviewSourceCount, engagementTotal, hasCreatorIdentity, hasObjectiveStats, overlay-zone area, etc.); runs validateInputAgainstTemplate as a hard filter; scores viable templates by signal richness; returns ranked [{template, viable, score, reasons[]}]. New route GET /api/layout/recommendations/:mediaId exposes it tenant-scoped. Per-template hard requirements: testimonial_spotlight needs any quote source; ugc_split_screen needs UGC context; review_collage needs ≥3 review sources / ≥4 quotes substrate; results_proof needs objective stats; testimonial_overlay needs usable hero + overlay zones + quote source; creator_endorsement needs creator identity (handle or named brand persona). PART 2 — Gemini theme prompt cleanup in layoutInputService.js. Drop theme.emphasis from schema + output shape (catalog is truth; Gemini's enum is misaligned with catalog — only 3 of 6 catalog emphasis values are in the Gemini enum, making the field broken-by-construction for half the templates). Enrich theme_style (6 values) and background_style (5 values) with concrete definitions in the prompt and reference the source image as the primary basis for style decisions. Bump INPUT_SCHEMA_VERSION to invalidate cached LayoutInputArtifact docs (re-derive on next preview visit). PREREQUISITE: complete canonical input field-by-field review (theme audited; brand/product/creator/ugc/social_proof/performance/cta/trust/copy/layout_options/defaults pending). Out of scope here: frontend recommendation UI (separate ticket); per-brand template-pinning override; telemetry on user-pick-vs-recommendation diff.

Summary: Matching service fortification — Phase 1.6/1.7 catalog-first per-product matching + class-aware NMS
Description: NEXT PRIORITY (start of next session). Bundled architectural shift across yolo_microservice + backend. Three coordinated changes in one PR set: (A) yolo_microservice/yolo_service.py — class-aware NMS in merge_nms. YOLO-vs-YOLO overlap stays tight (IoU 0.55); OpenCV-vs-OpenCV stays tight; YOLO-vs-OpenCV loosens to IoU 0.80 so OpenCV sub-region rectangles (e.g. clothing items inside a YOLO 'person' box) survive instead of being NMS-suppressed. ~5-line change in merge_nms. (B) PHASE 1.6 — services/cropRefineService.js (NEW). After Phase 1.5 non-product filtering, batch every surviving detection through one GPT-4.1 Vision call: 'given this crop and its identified label, return tight pixel coordinates of just the labeled item (1+ bboxes per input crop since a person crop may yield top + bottom + accessories).' Translate crop-relative bboxes back to source-image coords. Persist as DetectionArtifact.refinedProducts[] alongside yoloProducts (additive — yoloProducts stays for audit). Fallback: if refinement fails, downstream uses original yoloProducts bboxes. (C) PHASE 1.7 — productMatchService.js per-product catalog-first restructure. Schema: SWITCH TO MULTIPLE ProductMatchArtifact docs per detect run (option b — one artifact per refined product). Add productIndex field to artifact. Add Media.latestArtifacts.matches[] alongside singular .match (singular = highest-combined-score primary; backward-compat). Per-product flow: (1) findCatalogMatch (text scoring — existing) per refinedProduct seeded with refinedProduct.identification; (2) if textScore ≥ 0.5, new visualCatalogMatchService.js fires — Gemini Vision compares refined crop URL to top-K catalog candidate imageUrls, returns 'same product? confidence?'; (3) combined = max(textScore, visualScore); if combined ≥ 0.80 → catalog-winner, skip providers entirely for this detect run (run-scoped gate); (4) else → existing provider chain (Gemini grounded search + Lens + reasoner + decision tree). Multi-product detect outcome on Media.classification.detectSummary: aggregate — own_product if ANY match is own; competitor if ANY competitor and none own; etc. matchedProducts[] surfaces all per-match identifications. CASCADING UPDATES: pipelines/detect.js writes N artifacts + Media.latestArtifacts.matches[]; routes/detect.js assembleResult exposes productMatches singular (primary) + productMatches[] (full list); catalogProductDraftService fires one draft per match instead of one per run; instagramCommentService picks primary match by highest combined score; layoutInputService reads primary match for now (multi-product creative is a later concern). LOCKED DECISIONS: option b (multi-doc); Gemini Vision for visual catalog (not text-only first pass); one PR (1.6+1.7+NMS); provider gate at 0.80 combined. Effort: 4-6 hours careful code + smoke test on Pelagic Gear bikini media. PREREQUISITE FOR: Phase 0b (Media classification.detectSummary computation); resumption of canonical-data review (#80). Out of scope here: per-field provenance stamps on identification.details (Phase 3 follow-up); productDescriptionService.js Gemini description fetch (Phase 2 follow-up — only fires when catalog miss + provider win leaves description null, much rarer after this ticket); cross-provider second judge (#16); decision-tree disagreement telemetry (Phase 4 follow-up).

Refactor instagramCommentService quote-cascade to PREFER first-party post comments over Gemini external grounded search at every tier (product / category / brand). Summary: External Detect API v1 — review and ratify contract
Description: DRAFT contract for Lambda-driven external invocation of the detect pipeline. Full spec at server/docs/external-api-v1.md (canonical source — review there, not here). Summary: external app sends mediaUrl + brandId + optional pre-vectorized catalog (B2 pattern via vectorSetId) + catalogSource config; we return runId synchronously then deliver the assembled match results via webhook (or polling) when the run completes. Endpoints: POST /api/external/v1/detect, GET /api/external/v1/detect/:runId, POST/GET/DELETE /api/external/v1/catalogs/vector-sets[/:id], POST /api/external/v1/brands. Auth: Bearer API key (per-advertiser, hashed at rest, dailyQuota + 60req/min). Webhook signed with HMAC-SHA256 using caller-supplied callbackSecret; 3-attempt retry at 10s/60s/5min. Output payload includes per-refined-product matches with confidence scores (refined / reasoner / catalogCombined / catalogText / catalogVisual), full product hydration (title/imageUrl/productUrl/price/category/gtin/mpn) via catalog adapter, evidence (cropped image + bbox + label + agreement type + provider URLs), enrichment (rating/reviews/categoryReviews), run-level summary (own_product/competitor/mixed/category/no_products), and cost metadata. Open questions in the doc — embedding model registry, B1 vs B2 only, webhook retry policy, brand auto-provision races, cost metadata sensitivity, competitor suppression visibility, partial-results-on-failure. Dependencies: CatalogAdapter interface, ApiKey model + admin UI, webhook dispatch service, vector set storage, brand auto-provision extension. Action: review the doc, resolve open questions, then break into implementation Stories under a new Epic.

Summary: External Brand Enrichment API v1 — review and ratify contract
Description: DRAFT contract for Lambda-driven external brand provisioning + enrichment. Full spec at server/docs/external-api-v1.md (Brand Enrichment section). Summary: external app sends brand name + websiteUrl + optional curatedFields; we return brandId synchronously, kick off the four-stage enrichment chain (brandfetch → scraped → gpt → brand-reviews) in background, and deliver per-stage progress events + final brand record via signed webhook (or polling). Endpoints: POST /api/external/v1/brands, GET /api/external/v1/brands/:brandId, GET /api/external/v1/brands/:brandId/enrichment, POST /api/external/v1/brands/:brandId/enrichment/refresh, PATCH /api/external/v1/brands/:brandId. Pipeline mirrors internal brandEnrichmentService stages exactly — Brandfetch (logo + colors + fonts), homepage HTML scrape (theme color + fonts + GPT input text), GPT-4.1 (tagline + summary + tone + hashtags + tags + demographics + color/font fallbacks), Gemini grounded search (brandReviews quotes + rating + summary). Per-stage idempotency via Brand.enrichmentSources[]; per-field protection via Brand.curatedFields[]. Webhook events: brand.enrichment.stage-completed (fired N times, one per stage), brand.enrichment.completed (final), brand.enrichment.failed (unrecoverable error only — graceful per-stage failures land in stagesFailed[]). Synchronous waitForCompletion option for callers that need the enriched brand inline (max 90s block, fallback to async). PATCH endpoint for setting curatedFields[] overrides that future re-enrichment respects. Brand-detect integration: detect.brand{} inline shape triggers the same provisioning pipeline in background so detect doesn't block on enrichment. Action: review the doc, resolve open questions (waitForCompletion timeout, per-stage event volume, costMetadata visibility, refresh forcing on cache TTL), then break into implementation Stories under the same External API Epic as the detect contract.

Summary: ExtAPI-1: ApiKey model + Bearer middleware + rate limit + daily quota
Description: Foundation. New collection ApiKey { keyHash (sha256), keyPrefix (first 8 chars for display), advertiserId, brandId? (default), name, scopes[], dailyQuota, callsToday, callsTotal, lastUsedAt, createdAt, revokedAt }. Plaintext key shown ONCE at issue, never again. Middleware middleware/apiKeyAuth.js: extract Bearer header, sha256, lookup, set req.advertiserId + default req.brandId, increment callsToday counter, enforce dailyQuota (429 quota_exceeded), enforce per-minute rate limit (60 req/min, 429 rate_limited). All /api/external/v1/* routes mount this middleware. Cross-tenant guard: if request specifies a brandId outside the key's advertiser, reject 403 cross_tenant_brand. Rate limit headers in response: X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset.

Summary: ExtAPI-2: Admin UI for API key management
Description: Brand-level admin page at /admin/api-keys (or under brand settings). Issue new key (shows plaintext once with copy-to-clipboard + warning that it won't be shown again), list keys (prefix only + name + dailyQuota + callsToday + lastUsedAt), edit name/quota, revoke (sets revokedAt — middleware rejects revoked keys with 401 key_revoked). Reuses Chakra components from the in-flight UI migration epic. Per-key usage chart (last 30 days) for spotting runaway consumers.

Summary: ExtAPI-3: Webhook dispatch service + HMAC signing + retry
Description: Foundation. New services/webhookDispatchService.js: dispatch(event, payload, { url, secret, deliveryId }) — POST signed payload with X-LR-Signature: sha256=<hex>, X-LR-Event, X-LR-Run-Id (or X-LR-Brand-Id), X-LR-Delivery-Id headers. Retry with exponential backoff: attempts at 10s, 60s, 5min on consumer 5xx or timeout. Persist delivery attempts on a WebhookDelivery collection { deliveryId, runId/brandId, url, payloadDigest, attempts: [{ at, status, errorMessage }], status: 'pending' | 'delivered' | 'dead' }. Dead deliveries surface in admin UI for manual retry. Hook into pipelines/detect.js finalize phase + brandEnrichmentService stage completion + final completion. Detect endpoint side: webhook config persisted on DetectRun.delivery (added to schema in this story).

Summary: ExtAPI-4: Stable error envelope + error code registry
Description: Foundation. middleware/externalErrorEnvelope.js: catches errors thrown by /api/external/* routes, maps to { error: { code, message, field?, docsUrl }, requestId } shape. Stable error codes registered in errors/codes.js with HTTP status mapping: unauthorized (401), key_revoked (401), quota_exceeded (429), rate_limited (429), invalid_brand (400), invalid_vector_set (404), embedding_model_unsupported (400), image_fetch_failed (422), image_too_large (413), payload_too_large (413), idempotency_conflict (409), cross_tenant_brand (403), gemini_quota_exceeded (502), serpapi_quota_exceeded (502). docsUrl points at https://docs.liquidretail.app/errors/<code> (docs site separate ticket). All 4xx/5xx responses from external routes go through this envelope.

Summary: ExtAPI-5: SSRF-guarded image fetch service
Description: Foundation. New services/safeImageFetch.js: fetchImage(url, { maxBytes }) — validates URL is HTTPS (rejects http/file/data/etc.), resolves hostname and rejects private IPs (10.x, 172.16-31.x, 192.168.x, 127.x, 169.254.x, IPv6 fc00::/7, ::1), enforces 15s connect + read timeout, enforces maxBytes (default 10MB) via streaming abort, returns Buffer + mimeType. Caller-friendly error codes: image_invalid_url, image_fetch_failed (network/timeout/non-image content-type), image_too_large. Used by /api/external/v1/detect for media URL ingestion before Cloudinary upload. Rationale: external callers can pass arbitrary URLs; without SSRF guard, attackers could probe internal infrastructure (AWS metadata service, internal Render services, etc.).

Summary: ExtAPI-6: CatalogAdapter interface + MongoCatalogAdapter
Description: Detect surface foundation. New services/catalogAdapters/CatalogAdapter.js abstract base: searchByText({ brandId, query, category, limit }) → candidates[], getById(externalId) → product, listCategories(brandId) → categories[]. New services/catalogAdapters/MongoCatalogAdapter.js: refactor of existing inline queries in productMatchService.findCatalogMatchByText (moves Mongo-specific filtering + scoring behind the interface; existing matching service uses adapter via dependency injection). Brand model gains catalogSource: { type: 'mongo' | 'shopify' | 'meta' | 'rest', config: Mixed, credentialRef: String? } block (default {type:'mongo'}). Matching service resolves the adapter from brand.catalogSource at run time. No behavior change for existing brands; sets up the contract for non-mongo adapters.

Summary: ExtAPI-7: CatalogVectorSet model + lifecycle endpoints
Description: New model CatalogVectorSet { setId (vs_<brandSlug>_<hash>), advertiserId, brandId, embeddingModel, dim, modality (image | text | both), externalIds: [String], vectors: Buffer (binary float32 — externalIds.length × dim × 4 bytes), productCount, sizeBytes, createdAt, expiresAt, lastUsedAt }. Routes: POST /api/external/v1/catalogs/vector-sets (validates embeddingModel against EMBEDDING_MODELS registry, validates dim matches model spec, accepts vectors as JSON array OR base64-encoded float32 — base64 for payload efficiency), GET /:setId (metadata only, not vectors), DELETE /:setId. Storage strategy: Buffer field on Mongo doc up to 10MB (covers ~3.5k products at 768-dim). Above that, push to S3 with bucket pointer on the doc. TTL index on expiresAt for auto-cleanup.

Summary: ExtAPI-8: Vector match service (cosine sim against stored sets)
Description: New services/vectorMatchService.js: matchByVector({ vectorSetId, queryVector, topK }) → ranked candidates [{ externalId, score }]. Loads CatalogVectorSet, decodes Float32Array view of the stored Buffer, computes cosine similarity against queryVector (typed-array math; ~50ms for 10k × 768-dim). Caches the decoded Float32Array per setId in process memory (LRU, max 5 sets) so back-to-back detect runs against the same brand don't re-decode. embedRefinedCrop({ refined, embeddingModel }) helper that calls the appropriate provider (CLIP via Replicate or self-hosted, OpenAI text-embedding-3-large for text-only models, etc.) — provider registry follows EMBEDDING_MODELS interface. Replaces the existing visualCatalogMatchService Gemini-Vision-per-candidate path when a vectorSetId is supplied; falls back to existing path for legacy/Mongo-only brands.

Summary: ExtAPI-9: POST /api/external/v1/detect endpoint + DetectRun integration
Description: Headline detect entry point. Validates payload against schema (media[] required, brand{} required either as brandId or auto-provision metadata, catalog{} optional, pipeline{} tuning, delivery{} webhook config). For each media item: SSRF-guarded image fetch (ExtAPI-5), Cloudinary upload, Media upsert on (source: 'external', externalId), DetectRun.create with delivery config persisted. Worker picks up the run via existing queue. 202 response with runs[] including statusUrl + webhookConfigured + estimatedCompletionMs. Idempotency key: header X-Idempotency-Key takes precedence; falls back to (apiKey, media[].externalId) tuple. Repeat requests within 24h return the same response without queueing a new run.

Summary: ExtAPI-10: GET /api/external/v1/detect/:runId polling endpoint
Description: Polling fallback for callers without a webhook receiver. Returns same shape as the webhook payload — current status (pending | running | completed | failed), current stage, elapsedMs, estimatedRemainingMs, plus the full result payload when status is completed | failed. assembleExternalResult() helper in services/externalResultService.js: takes a DetectRun + Media + artifacts, returns the curated subset described in the contract (matches[] with scores, product hydration via CatalogAdapter, evidence, enrichment, run-level summary, costMetadata). Excludes internal Mongo ObjectIds; uses brand-supplied externalId for catalog references.

Summary: ExtAPI-11: ShopifyCatalogAdapter implementation
Description: First non-Mongo CatalogAdapter. New services/catalogAdapters/ShopifyCatalogAdapter.js using Shopify Storefront GraphQL API (read-only). searchByText: products(query: ..., first: limit) returning { externalId (gid://shopify/Product/...), title, imageUrl (featuredImage.url), brand (vendor), category (productType), productUrl (onlineStoreUrl), price (priceRange.minVariantPrice), gtin (variants.barcode). getById: node(id: gid://...) lookup. Auth via brand.catalogSource.config.credentialRef pointing at AWS Secrets Manager / Render env var with the shop domain + Storefront access token. Handles Shopify rate limits (cost-based, 50pt bucket) with backoff. Catalog browser admin tab gains a 'Connect Shopify' button that writes the catalogSource block.

Summary: ExtAPI-12: Cost metadata collection through pipeline
Description: Wire usageMetadata.totalTokenCount from every Gemini call + usage.total_tokens from every OpenAI call + counter for SerpAPI calls into a per-DetectRun cost ledger. New DetectRun.costLedger field: { geminiTokensInput, geminiTokensOutput, openaiTokensInput, openaiTokensOutput, serpApiCalls, geminiImageGens, approxCostUsd }. Each provider service (geminiSearchProvider, productDetailsService, googleLensProvider, etc.) accepts an optional costAccumulator argument; pipeline.detect.js threads one through every call. assembleExternalResult includes costLedger in the costMetadata block when delivery.include contains 'costMetadata'. Same accumulator pattern reused by brandEnrichmentService for the branding API's costMetadata.

Summary: ExtAPI-13: POST /api/external/v1/brands + per-stage webhook events
Description: Branding entry point. Validates body (name + websiteUrl required, optional curatedFields/pipeline/delivery). Idempotent on (advertiserId, normalized name + url) — returns existing Brand if found unless pipeline.skipIfExists=false. Kicks off enrichBrandFromUrl in background, returns 202 with brandId + stagesPlanned. Extends brandEnrichmentService.runEnrichment to accept optional delivery config: at the end of EACH stage's setStage call, fires brand.enrichment.stage-completed webhook via the dispatcher (ExtAPI-3) with { stage, fields, fieldsLockedByCuration, elapsedMs }. End of run fires brand.enrichment.completed (or .failed). Curated overrides supplied in the request body are immediately added to Brand.curatedFields[] before enrichment starts so the GPT/Brandfetch stages respect them. POST /api/external/v1/brands/:brandId/enrichment/refresh: clears Brand.enrichmentSources[] and re-runs the full chain (or specified stages).

Summary: ExtAPI-14: waitForCompletion synchronous mode for /brands
Description: When request body has pipeline.waitForCompletion=true, server holds the response until enrichment finishes (max 90s). Implementation: createPromise, register a one-shot listener on the brand-enrichment event emitter keyed by brandId, await with timeout. On completion → 200 with full brand record (same shape as the .completed webhook). On timeout → 202 fallback with statusUrl so caller can poll. On failure → 502 with the .failed event body. Useful for callers that need enriched colors before downstream ad assembly. Emitter pattern: brandEnrichmentService gains an EventEmitter that runEnrichment publishes 'stage-completed' / 'completed' / 'failed' events to, keyed by brandId. The webhook dispatcher and the wait-for-completion handler both subscribe.

Summary: ExtAPI-15: GET /brands/:id/enrichment + PATCH /brands/:id curated overrides
Description: Polling endpoint and curation endpoint. GET /api/external/v1/brands/:brandId/enrichment returns the enrichment status (pending | running | completed | failed), currentStage, stagesCompleted/pending/skipped/failed[], startedAt, elapsedMs, estimatedRemainingMs. When status is completed/failed, includes the full brand record (or error). PATCH /api/external/v1/brands/:brandId accepts { curated: { field: value, ... } } and writes through to Brand model + adds the field names to Brand.curatedFields[] so future re-enrichment skips them. Validates field names against an allowlist (no PATCH-ing of advertiserId, _id, etc.). Returns the updated Brand record + the full curatedFields[] list. Companion GET /brands/:brandId returns the current Brand record without triggering enrichment.

Summary: Phase A-0: Detect-pipeline derivations for Media Library insights (backend prereq)
Description: Backend prereq for Phase A-2 frontend Media Library work. Adds derived insights at the end of the detect pipeline so the media library can render Ad Readiness, Mood, Scene Type, concise primary subject label, and sharpness without on-the-fly recomputation. New fields on Media: adSuitability.score (0-10 composite) and adSuitability.reasons[] (typed bullets {kind, label, severity}); background.mood[] (2-4 adjectives), background.sceneType (e.g. 'Outdoor Trail'), background.timeOfDayLabel (mapped from existing background.lighting); primarySubjectLabel (concise — e.g. 'Person (Runner)'), secondaryElementsTags[]; technicalInsights.{brightnessAvg, densityAvg, focusScore, focusBucket}. Implementation: (1) extend the existing subject-text GPT prompt to ALSO emit primarySubjectLabel + secondaryElementsTags + mood + sceneType (same call, ~50 extra output tokens). (2) New services/imageQualityService.js: computeFocus(buf) → Laplacian variance via sharp's convolve filter; bucket: <100 Soft, 100-300 Acceptable, >300 Sharp. (3) New services/adSuitabilityService.js: scoreMedia(media) → {score, reasons[]} via rule-based composite — refined product confidence, primary subject prominence, brightness + density + focus signals, overlay-zone safe-area ratio, text-on-subject penalty, competitor outcome penalty. (4) Pipeline finalize stage calls all three and writes to Media. Closes the existing backlog row 'adSuitability scoring writer' (#28). Files: pipelines/detect.js, services/subjectTextService.js (prompt extension), NEW services/imageQualityService.js, NEW services/adSuitabilityService.js, models/Media.js (schema additions). Effort: ~1.5 days.

Summary: Phase A-1: Media Library page — canvas + sidebar + base overlays
Description: New /media-library route in the Chakra app. Out-of-band Phase A precursor to the Phase 6 detect rebuild — this page is also a Phase 6 dependency since it surfaces the same media list + per-media artifact data. Reuses Phases 1-3 infrastructure: PipelineShell, useBrand, apiFetch. SCOPE: (a) left rail paginated Media list scoped to active brand — thumbnail, title (caption first 50 chars or filename), source pill (Instagram/Manual upload/etc.), match-level pill (High/Medium/Low/None — derived from Media.matchedProducts[0].outcome), time ago, video indicator. Pagination + filter by source type. (b) Main canvas: selected media's image with bbox overlay layers — Products (refinedProducts), People (yoloProducts.className=person), Text (text[]), Safe Zones (overlayZones.restrictions inverted as safe areas), Density (overlayZones.densityGrid as heatmap), Crops (smartCrops bounding outlines), Palette (color swatches). All toggleable via filter chips above the canvas. (c) Aspect ratio strip below canvas — Original + 1:1 + 4:5 + 9:16 + 1.91:1 + 16:9 (note: 16:9 depends on existing backlog row 'Add 16:9 to extendedCropsService'); each variant shows a quality pill bucketed from the judge winnerScore (≥0.80 High, ≥0.60 Medium, else Low). (d) Top metadata strip: filename, source pill, creator handle, engagement counts (likes/comments — IG-sourced only, dash for manual), time ago, kebab menu. (e) Right sidebar with 6 tabs scaffolded (Summary, Objects, Crops, Text, Layout, Palette); only Summary tab populated MINIMALLY in this story with refinedProducts list + basic scene description — full Summary content lands in A-2. (f) Bottom action bar: Delete (existing cascadeDeleteMedia route), Continue to Ad Generation (routes to /ads with ?mediaId=). EXCLUDED: AI Readiness score + bullets, Mood, Scene Type, Detected Products card with match levels, agreement type, category breadcrumb, three-tier reviews, Collections, Request Rights, evidence drill-ins — all in A-2/A-3. Components: pages/media-library.tsx, components/MediaLibrary/{Sidebar, SidebarRow, Canvas, OverlayLayer/*, FilterChips, AspectRatioStrip, MediaHeader, BottomBar}.tsx. Effort: ~3 days.

Summary: Phase A-2: Media Library — AI Summary + Detected Products + Scene & Subjects + Technical Insights tabs
Description: Right-sidebar content for the Media Library page. DEPENDS ON Phase A-0 backend derivations being in place. Each tab maps to a section of the hifi mockup. SCOPE: (a) Summary tab: AI Readiness score (0-10) with 1-decimal display + readiness bullets list (Strong product visibility / Clean safe overlay zones / Good lighting on subject / Slight text on rock — each derived from Media.adSuitability.reasons[]) + 'View Suggestions' button opening a slide-over with detailed remediation copy per flagged bullet. Below: Detected Products mini-list with title, match % (rounded), match-level pill (outcome→bucket), agreement type chip (agree/category-confirmed/single-engine/catalog), and category breadcrumb (resolved via productMatchHydration). Below: Scene & Subjects panel with Primary Subject (Media.primarySubjectLabel), Secondary Elements (Media.secondaryElementsTags joined), Scene Type (Media.background.sceneType), Mood (Media.background.mood joined), Time of Day (Media.background.timeOfDayLabel). Below: Technical Insights row — Brightness % (Media.technicalInsights.brightnessAvg × 100), Clutter (Media.technicalInsights.densityAvg bucketed Low/Medium/High), Focus (Media.technicalInsights.focusBucket); each with a Good/OK/Poor quality dot derived from per-metric thresholds. Below: collapsible Raw AI Data section dumping the assembled artifact JSON for debugging. (b) Objects tab: full per-detection list with bbox preview, label, brand, category, confidence, agreement type. (c) Crops tab: smart + extended crops as a grid with judge scores. (d) Text tab: OCR detections list with content, type (brand/product_label/other), confidence, bbox preview. (e) Layout tab: per-aspect-ratio overlay zones — primary subject rect, restriction rects with strictness, density grid + brightness grid mini visualizations. (f) Palette tab: color swatches from Media.background.palette + dominant-color cluster bars. ADDITIONAL: detectSummary outcome badge on canvas header (own_product=green, competitor=red, mixed=yellow, category=blue, no_products=gray). Components: components/MediaLibrary/Tabs/{Summary,Objects,Crops,Text,Layout,Palette}.tsx, components/MediaLibrary/{OutcomeBadge,ReadinessBullet,SuggestionsSlideOver}.tsx. Effort: ~3 days.

Summary: Phase A-3: Media Library — Collections + per-product evidence drill-ins + three-tier reviews
Description: Net-new feature work + drill-in detail surfaces. SCOPE: (a) Collection model + CRUD: NEW model models/Collection.js {brandId, advertiserId, name, mediaIds[], createdAt, updatedAt} with (brandId, name) unique compound index. Routes: POST /api/collections (create), GET /api/collections?brandId= (list scoped to brand), PATCH /api/collections/:id (rename), DELETE /api/collections/:id, POST /api/collections/:id/media (add media — accepts mediaIds[] for batch), DELETE /api/collections/:id/media/:mediaId (remove). Cascade: when a Media is deleted via cascadeDeleteMedia, pull its id from any Collection.mediaIds via Mongoose post-remove middleware so collections never reference dead media. (b) Frontend AddToCollectionMenu in the bottom action bar: dropdown listing the brand's collections + 'Create new collection' inline. Multi-select on the sidebar enables batch add. (c) CollectionsManager modal: list/edit/delete collections, see member count + last-updated, click into a collection to filter the Media Library sidebar to just that collection's members. (d) EvidencePopover: clicking the agreement chip on a Detected Product opens a popover showing the providers that fired (gemini-search, google-lens, catalog), each provider's evidence URLs with thumbnails, reasoner reasoning text, and the per-engine confidence — sourced from ProductMatchArtifact.providers (server-only data; not currently exposed via productMatchHydration — extend the hydration helper to optionally include providers when ?include=evidence). (e) ReviewsSlideOver: clicking a Detected Product opens a three-tier review surface — Product Reviews (CatalogProduct.productReviews), Category Reviews (Category.categoryReviews via categoryId), Brand Reviews (Brand.brandReviews) — quotes + ratings + sources for each tier. (f) Request Rights button: separate from this story; tracked under existing backlog row 'Dedicated rights management screen' (#29). Components: NEW models/Collection.js, NEW routes/collections.js, components/MediaLibrary/{AddToCollectionMenu,CollectionsManager,EvidencePopover,ReviewsSlideOver}.tsx. Effort: ~2.5 days.

Summary: Real ad-render previews replacing PreviewCard placeholder
Description: Phase 4 follow-up #7. Replace the static brand-page PreviewCard mock layout with a real RenderArtifact thumbnail. Depends on Phase 1 render service shipping. Hook the same /api/render endpoint the Creatives gallery uses; pick a representative product+template pair per brand.

Summary: Generate Ads wizard — wire backend
Description: Hook the new Generate Ads wizard's Step 1 to GET /api/campaigns?brandId=X (filtered by syncedAt), Step 2 to a per-campaign filtered catalog endpoint (products detected in any media linked to the campaign's productSetIds), Step 3 to a templates-list endpoint, Step 4 to POST /api/ads/generate. Today the wizard ships skeleton-only — empty states + step state machine — pending these endpoints.

Summary: Swap Puppeteer to @sparticuz/chromium-min for render service
Description: Current postinstall pulls the full Chrome binary into Render's build cache (~150MB, ~30s deploy slowdown). @sparticuz/chromium-min ships a slimmer Chromium tuned for serverless/limited-memory hosts and avoids the postinstall download — better fit for the Render free tier. Swap puppeteer.launch() to use chromium.executablePath() and chromium.args, gate behind a NODE_ENV check so local dev still uses the regular puppeteer install. Validate render output is byte-identical and Cloudinary upload still succeeds.

Summary: Extract render service into its own Render-hosted microservice
Description: Ship the Puppeteer renderService as a standalone repo (Docker, chromium preinstalled in the base image, no .puppeteerrc / postinstall hooks needed) following the YOLO microservice pattern (madecastro/yolo_microservice.git). Service contract mirrors the existing renderCreative req: { campaignRunId, brandId, campaignId, campaignKind, creative, cta, options } → { status, jobId, ad? | error? }. The campaign API stays in the main backend and POSTs to the render service over HTTP; auth threading switches from RENDER_AUTH_TOKEN env to a request-scoped JWT forwarded by the API. Persistence stays in the main backend (render service returns the rendered bytes / Cloudinary upload result; API persists the Ad doc) so we keep a single source of truth for tenant scoping and de-dupe.

Summary: Track Ad.campaignRunIds[] for multi-run de-dupe surfacing
Description: Today Ad.campaignRunId is a single string set at creation time. When a re-render hits the (campaignId, derivationDigest) dedupe, the cached Ad keeps its ORIGINAL runId — so the /ads page filtered by the new runId comes back empty even though dedupe technically succeeded. Migrate Ad.campaignRunId → Ad.campaignRunIds[] (array, indexed); on dedupe hit, $addToSet the current runId; change /ads filter from `runId === X` to `runIds includes X`. Existing docs migrate via a one-shot script that wraps the scalar into a single-element array. Once this lands, smoke-test refresh:true can drop back to dedupe-by-default behavior since the gallery will surface dedupe hits correctly.

Summary: Render service auth: replace static RENDER_AUTH_TOKEN env with request-scoped service JWT
Description: Today the renderService authenticates inside the Puppeteer page by seeding localStorage.auth_token from a long-lived RENDER_AUTH_TOKEN env var. Two problems: (1) the JWT expires periodically and every render then 401s until an operator manually refreshes the env value, (2) all renders run as whichever user happened to copy their token into the env, regardless of who triggered the campaign run. Switch to issuing a short-lived, machine-scoped JWT per render request — signed by the API server with a service identity claim that requireAuth recognizes — and pass it to renderService as part of the renderCreative request. The Puppeteer launch seeds it into localStorage same as today, but the token is fresh on every call and expires in minutes. Acceptance: token expiration no longer causes silent 35s timeouts; CampaignRun.requestedBy correctly tracks who initiated the render even when the API and render service are split (anticipating the render-service-extraction work).

Summary: Ad creation matching logic — reference doc
Description: Source of truth: ProductMatchArtifact (PMA) per (mediaId, matched-product), written by detect pipeline. Branch in services/campaignAdsGenerationService.expandWizardJob: kind='brand' OR (no products + no media) → seedFromBrandOnly (top 5 brand_match PMAs by Media.adSuitability). mediaIds present → seedFromMedia: dispatch by PMA.outcome (product_match → catalogProductId; product_category → first recommendedProducts[] entry or first sibling in PMA.categoryId; brand_match → productId:null). productIds present → seedsFromProduct: top product_match PMAs by suitability for that productId, fallback to brand_match (productId stays for tracking). Both → union, dedupe by (productId|null, mediaId). Cartesian: seed × template × shipping ratio in {1:1, 9:16, 16:9}. Capped at MAX_CREATIVES_PER_RUN. Cross-direction picker UX reads same data: media → matchedProducts[]; product → ProductMatchArtifact.find({catalogProductId, outcome:'product_match'}).sort(suitability).

Summary: UI for re-match trigger
Description: Surface POST /api/detect/rematch in the operator UI. On the brand status panel show 'X media without product match' alongside a 'Re-match' button. Optional secondary action on the media library (per-row 'Re-match' action) for one-off retries. Backend route exists already; this card is just the affordance. Default behavior: tenant-scoped, fileType-optional filter, capped at 50 per click; explicit-list path lets per-row triggers send a single mediaId.

Summary: Category-as-seed in the Generate Ads wizard
Description: Today the wizard accepts productIds and mediaIds. Matches that resolve a Category leaf but no CatalogProduct (rare — ensureCatalogProductForMatch usually drafts one) land only on Media.matchedCategories and Category.relatedMedia. Make these matches actionable: (1) enrich Category.matchedMedia[] with { mediaId, matchTier, confidence, refinedProductId, matchEvidenceArtifactId, matchedAt } mirroring CatalogProduct.matchedMedia. (2) Mirror writes in detect.mirrorMatchesToCategories alongside the existing product mirror. (3) Wizard accepts categoryIds; new seedsFromCategory emits ugc seeds per matched media. (4) Ad doc gains categoryId alongside productId so attribution survives. (5) Wizard picker UI surfaces a category chip alongside the product/media chips. Mostly relevant for no-catalog brands where reasoner returned null but productCategoryService resolved a leaf.

Summary: Cost optimization review — onboarding ingest
Description: After template variant wiring (variantKind threading, slot gating, template whitelist) lands, revisit the per-Media ingest cost. Baseline (2026-05-11): $35-50 for ~100 products + 200 catalog images + 50 IG posts. Dominant line items: (1) extended-crops Gemini image gen (~$0.10-0.30 per Media, runs on every Media in lazy chain), (2) provider fallback when catalog-first <0.80 (~$0.05 per refined product), (3) new multi-image visual catalog matching (4x Gemini calls per text candidate). Levers to evaluate: gate extended-crops on adSuitability threshold (skip low-quality Media); raise catalog-first hit threshold tradeoff vs miss-rate; tune multi-image catalog comparison to top-N catalog crops per candidate instead of all. Measure actual bills vs the $35-50 estimate before deciding which lever to pull.

Summary: Catalog product video ingest
Description: Pipeline side already handles thumbnail-first hero selection for any Media with metadata.thumbnailUrl set — works for catalog product videos automatically. Ingest side gaps: (1) catalogProductDetectService.materializeImage hardcodes fileType=image; needs a materializeVideo path that sets fileType=video + metadata.thumbnailUrl from the source feed poster. (2) Shopify catalog sync (catalogSyncService) needs to detect product.media[].mediaContentType=VIDEO entries with previewImage.url as poster. (3) IG Commerce catalog needs the equivalent video_url + image_url poster handling. (4) catalogProductDetectService.enqueueProductDetect alt-image loop currently limited to MAX_ALT_IMAGES and image-only; expand to mixed image+video gallery items. Defer until first brand actually ships catalog videos in their feed.

Summary: OAI-first hero selection for catalog products
Description: Currently catalogProductDetectService enqueues a separate DetectRun for hero + every alt image, running full YOLO + Gemini stack on each. For brands with 3-5 alts per product this multiplies catalog ingest cost. Proposal: send all catalog images for one product to gpt-4o-mini in a single call to pick the cleanest product shot, run full detect only on that winner. Alts get a minimal Media doc (Cloudinary mirror + metadata) without YOLO/Gemini. Trade-off: loses the multi-image visual catalog matching coverage shipped 2026-05-11 (matching falls back to hero-only). Worth building when we have data on (a) actual multi-image matching hit-rate gains and (b) typical alt-count distribution per brand. Estimated savings: 5-15 dollars per 100-product ingest.

Summary: Carousel-aware seed expansion in seedsFromMedia
Description: seedsFromMedia treats every post as single-asset. When the operator picks an IG carousel post, the cartesian should expand by each carousel child (each becomes a separate hero candidate) × matched products × paletteSource — grows exponentially but each carousel image gives the operator a distinct visual. Blocked on ingestion: postSyncService:10 takes only the first carousel child today (Carousels: V1 takes only the first child item as the primary media). Two options for the ingestion change: (A) materialize each child as its own Media doc with its own DetectRun — cleanest but doubles+ Media count for carousel-heavy brands; (B) store children URLs on the parent Media metadata and reference by index in the seed — keeps Media count flat but seeds carry a non-Media reference shape templates can't directly bind. Recommend A and accept the storage hit. Add MAX_ADS_PER_GENERATION_RUN guard against runaway expansion (already in place at 200).

Summary: Unify template schemas — migrate overlay templates into canvas.v1.json
Description: Today template geometry lives in TWO schemas: canvas.v1.json (for canvas-mode templates: testimonial_spotlight, ugc_split_screen, review_collage, results_proof, creator_endorsement — rigid rect per ratio) and templates.normalized.json (for overlay-mode templates: testimonial_overlay, product_overlay — placement_policy.element_priority_order computes rects at render time via OverlayZoneArtifact + greedy placement). The renderer already converges them at the DOM layer (single tp-zone kind-X style-Y system) but the upstream zone declarations live in two places. Drift is inevitable — already caused a doc/render mismatch on ugc_split_screen's product_meta (2026-05-13). Refactor: (1) Migrate overlay templates' zone declarations INTO canvas.v1.json with placement_mode:'adaptive' on zones whose rect is computed at render. (2) Strip zones / render_order / background_binding / placement_policy.element_priority_order from templates.normalized.json — keep style_bindings, validation, slot_adapter, truncation_rules, motion_policy, fallback_policy. (3) Unify templatePreview.js's two zone-loading paths into a single loadZones(template, ratio) that post-processes adaptive zones through the placement service. (4) Update validateInputAgainstTemplate to introspect canvas. Size: ~400-600 lines added to canvas, ~150 stripped from templates spec, ~50 line renderer change, ~30 line validator change. Trigger to do: adding a 5th overlay template, a renderer change that needs to touch both paths, or a new contributor getting confused. Rule going forward (until refactored): new templates that aren't full-bleed overlays use canvas-first. Any new full-bleed overlay keeps placement_policy in templates spec.

Summary: UGC Management — tagged-posts ingestion + rights workflow + brand-voice agent
Description: Epic for the UGC Management page: pull tagged posts from IG, pre-screen for repost candidacy without running the full detect pipeline, surface them on a new top-level page (alongside Detect Review), allow operators to approve rights manually, and (V3) ship a brand-voice AI agent that drafts outreach comments + interprets creator replies behind a human-in-the-loop gate. Approved media flows into the existing Media Library (rights.approved=true is the existing gate) and becomes selectable in the Generate Ads wizard. Three phases below. Detect pipeline is GATED on rights.status=approved — UGC media never enters detect until permission is granted (cost discipline). Per-brand context, NOT per-brand agent instances — single shared service with Brand.tone/summary/hashtags + uploadSettings.rightsOutreachTemplate as the system-prompt context.

Summary: UGC Phase 1: tagged-posts sync + management page + manual rights flip + Tier 1+2 pre-screen
Description: Ship tagged-posts ingestion (/{ig-user-id}/tags) WITHOUT enqueuing DetectRun. Media stamps classification.socialPostType=ugc + metadata.creatorHandle + metadata.creatorIgUserId. Extend Media.rights with: status (enum: synced/screening/outreach_drafted/outreach_sent/awaiting_response/response_received/approval_drafted/approved/decline_drafted/declined/not_pursuing), candidacyScore (0-1), candidacyReasons[], prescreenAt. Keep existing approved/approvedAt mirroring status=approved for the existing media-library gate. New ugcPrescreenService runs Tier 1 (free signals: hashtag match against Brand.hashtags, brand mention in caption, engagement floor, recency, media-type filter, caption length) + Tier 2 (NER on caption via existing nerService + Gemini Flash one-shot classifier). Auto-skips to not_pursuing when score < 0.2. Wire tagged sync into integrations.js IG finalize + onboarding.js dispatch-syncs + scheduledSyncService alongside the existing posts sync. Detect gate: postSyncService and post-rematch-after-catalog skip dispatch when socialPostType=ugc && rights.status!==approved. New routes: GET /api/ugc list + PATCH /api/ugc/:mediaId/rights-status manual flip. New frontend page at /ugc in SECONDARY_NAV between Detect Review and Media Library — tile grid with thumbnail/creator/permalink/candidacy badge/status pill/engagement, filters by status/score/recency, per-tile Approve manually + Skip + Request rights (textarea placeholder until V3), side drawer with caption + candidacy reasons + engagement + status controls.

Summary: UGC Phase 2: pre-screen refinements + Cloudinary categorization + bulk operations
Description: Consume Cloudinary categorization tags returned at ingest (free — Imagga via Cloudinary, no extra API call) and surface as filter facets on the UGC page (e.g., food/kitchen/person). Add Brand.uploadSettings.candidacyMinScore + autoNotPursuingBelow operator-tunable thresholds. Bulk operations on the UGC page: skip-all-below-threshold + draft-outreach-for-all-above-threshold (V3-conditional). Optional Tier 4: per-tile Run vision screen button — one Gemini Flash vision call for borderline candidates (operator-triggered, not auto). Cost discipline: vision pass is opt-in per tile, not run on the whole batch.

Summary: UGC Phase 3: brand-voice AI agent + state machine + conversation history
Description: New UgcConversation collection keyed on (brandId, mediaId, creatorIgUserId) with messages[]: direction (outbound/inbound), channel (comment/dm — V3 ships comment-only since instagram_manage_comments is already granted; DM needs instagram_manage_messages re-OAuth), content, draftedByAgent, draftedAt, sentAt, externalCommentId, parsedIntent, parsedConfidence. Add Brand.uploadSettings.rightsOutreachTemplate operator-editable system-prompt addendum. New ugcRightsAgentService: draftOutreach (composes first comment using Brand.name + tone[] + summary + template addendum), interpretReply (LLM classifies creator reply as approve/decline/clarification/unrelated + confidence + reasoning), composeFollowup (drafts clarifying reply for clarification intent). Extend instagramCommentService with postComment + fetchComments. Wire instagramWebhookService comments field handler — inbound comment → match to UgcConversation → trigger interpretReply → write approval_drafted or decline_drafted state. Human-in-the-loop at BOTH gates: operator approves outbound send (draft → outreach_sent) AND inbound interpretation (approval_drafted → approved). Routes: POST /api/ugc/:mediaId/draft-outreach + send-outreach + confirm-decision.
