Frontend additions: Draft outreach CTA → drawer with agent-drafted message → operator edits + sends; conversation drawer with full message log; banner Agent thinks the creator said YES (87% confidence) with Confirm + Reject buttons; auto-refresh on webhook delivery. Auto-send override off by default; per-brand toggle to enable once trust is established (inbound interpretation gate stays).

Summary: Team invitations: SendGrid auto-send
Description: V1 Team page (commit 53ed5fa) ships copy-invite-link — operator generates a link and pastes into Slack/email themselves. SendGrid account already exists. Wire an email-send step into POST /api/invitations: after the AdvertiserMembership row is created, fire a templated email to the invitee with the accept URL, the inviter's name, the workspace name, and the role they're being invited as. Keep copy-link path as a fallback when email send fails (already in the response payload). Add Brand.uploadSettings-style switch for auto-resend on duplicate-pending invite create (today we silently return the existing invite). Stamp invitedEmailSentAt + invitedEmailMessageId on the AdvertiserMembership for audit. SendGrid env vars: SENDGRID_API_KEY, SENDGRID_FROM_EMAIL, SENDGRID_FROM_NAME. Failure path: log + return the invite anyway so the operator can copy-link manually.

Summary: On-model product swap to expand cartesian inventory
Description: When a Media has shotType=on_model, run a service that swaps the worn/held product for a target product so any compatible product in the catalog can pair with that media seed (instead of the current 1:1 model/product binding). Two service paths with different maturity: (a) APPAREL VTON — Google Vertex AI Virtual Try-On, FASHN.ai, or Replicate-hosted IDM-VTON/OOTDiffusion. Mature, purpose-built for garment swap, $0.02-0.10/img; (b) CPG / OBJECT SWAP — no dedicated SaaS, do SAM2 mask + reference-guided inpaint with Gemini 2.5 Flash Image (Nano Banana) or Flux Kontext. Works for held bottles, packaged goods on counter; weak on legible brand text and complex occlusion (hand wrap). Cost-control architecture: do the swap ONCE per (productId, sourceMediaId) pair, cache the result as a Media (or MediaDerivative) with provenance pointing back to source, then the existing campaignAdsGenerationService cartesian × renderService matrix consumes it like any other media — keeps generative call count linear in (products × on-model media) rather than cartesian. Cartesian integration: new variantKind ugc_swap (or product_swap) in seedsFromProduct, gated by sourceMedia.classification.shotType==='on_model' and category compatibility between worn product and target product. Judge gate required per swap before it enters the queue — quality variance is too high to skip. Architecturally a Render Docker microservice per the established yolo_microservice / creative-render-service pattern (heavy/bursty/specialized GPU deps). Open questions before building: (1) apparel-only V1 vs CPG also from day one; (2) Vertex VTON vs FASHN.ai vs self-hosted on Replicate; (3) MediaDerivative collection vs flagging on Media with sourceMediaId/swapProductId; (4) judge model — reuse existing judgeService or specialized swap-quality prompt.

Summary: AI-as-layout-designer architecture (LLM emits canvas specs, renderer draws)
Description: Replace the current AI Layout Studio (gpt-image-1 generated pixels — distorted elements, hallucinated text) with an architecture where the LLM emits structured CANVAS SPECS in the same shape as schemas/rsSocialProof.canvas.v1.json and the existing deterministic renderer (templatePreview.js drawTpCanvas) draws the actual ad. Zero pixels from the LLM. INPUT TO LLM: full brand block (colors/logo/tone/font/tagline) + full product block (display-normalized name/image/price/rating/reviews/category/description) + full source_media block (url/palette/subjects/scene/mood/OCR) + copy candidates (multiple headlines/subheadlines/eyebrows) + full social_proof block (rating/review_count/verified_buyers/ALL quotes with author+source/review_summary) + creator block when UGC (handle/platform/follower_count/rights_status) + campaign block (offer/raffle) + available_media (hero_image/hero_video+poster+duration/lifestyle_image+video/ugc_image+video/alt_images/alt_videos) + canvas dims + platform + format + creative_style_preference (operator constraint or null=LLM picks). The LLM picks which elements to use per creative style — give everything, let it skip what doesn't support the chosen direction. ELEMENT CATALOG with REQUIRED zones (logo, cta, one of headline/product_card/quote_card) + OPTIONAL zones (support_media, panel, eyebrow_rules, proof_bar, quote_card, product_card, badge_row, creator_chip, offer_pill, secondary_media, scrim) — described in prompt with which data each requires. CREATIVE STYLE MENU: social_proof_led, brand_led, product_led, editorial, ugc_led, promotional — each with typical zones and skips. PLATFORM MENU with per-platform constraints in prompt: meta_feed (1:1, 4:5; polished; in-creative-headline OK), meta_reels/meta_stories (9:16; safe_top 220px / safe_bottom 300px; native feel; minimal chrome), tiktok (9:16; UGC-led dominates; video strongly preferred), pinterest (2:3; text-rich; lifestyle hero), linkedin (1.91:1, 1:1; professional), google_display (multiple ratios + IAB sizes 300x250/728x90/etc.; in-creative CTA), google_pmax_image (1.91:1/1:1/4:5; FORBIDS in-creative headline/cta — emits separate external_text_assets block instead with headlines[5-15]/long_headlines[1-5]/descriptions[1-5]/business_name/callouts), google_pmax_logo (1:1, 4:1; logo only), standard_display_iab (IAB sizes; heavy text + hard CTA OK). CAROUSEL FORMAT: meta_feed_carousel (2-10 cards 1:1 or 1.91:1, mixed media OK), meta_stories_carousel (2-10 9:16 frames ≤15s/video), tiktok_photo_carousel (up to 35 photos 9:16, image only), pinterest_idea_pin (up to 20 pages 9:16), linkedin_carousel (2-10 1.91:1), google_demand_gen_carousel (2-10 1:1/1.91:1). Carousel output: top-level cards[] array each with own canvas spec + card_role (hook/feature/proof/offer/cta) + narrative thread. Narrative menu: feature_showcase, multi_product, before_after, narrative_arc, testimonial_series, editorial_unfolding. Style_bindings must be identical across cards (visual consistency). VIDEO+IMAGE FIRST-CLASS: media zone gains media_kind:'image'|'video' field + poster_required flag. Renderer already picks media.video||media.image at templatePreview.js:2358-2378. Per-platform constraints tell LLM duration limits + when video is preferred (meta_reels/tiktok: video strongly preferred; pinterest/linkedin: image preferred but video allowed; google_pmax_image: image only — video is separate google_pmax_video format). Top-level media_usage summary: uses_video/uses_image/total_video_duration_sec. OUTPUT SCHEMA: same shape as canvas.v1.json variant + creative_style declaration + rationale + elements_used + elements_skipped + (carousel: cards[]) + (pmax/display: external_text_assets) + media_usage. VALIDATOR: zone bounds 0-1000 + slot/kind/style_variant whitelist + required-zones enforcement + elements_used must match zones[].id set + forbidden_zones per platform (e.g. headline forbidden on pmax_image) + safe_top/safe_bottom enforcement (zones can't intrude on platform UI reserved areas) + external_text_assets count ranges per platform + per-card validation for carousels + cross-card style_bindings consistency check + video duration within platform limits. RENDERER IMPACT: minimal for single creative (drawTpCanvas already takes spec+input). New carousel render endpoint takes sessionId+cardIndex returns rendered HTML for one card. CARTESIAN IMPACT: platform+format become campaign-level operator picks (bound the fanout per run). Carousel collapses N cards into ONE Ad doc not N. BUILD ORDER: Phase 1 = single creative + meta_feed (1:1, 4:5) + meta_reels (9:16) + image+video both. Phase 2 = tiktok. Phase 3 = meta_feed_carousel. Phase 4 = google_pmax_image + external_text_assets. Phase 5 = stories/tiktok carousels. Phase 6 = pinterest/linkedin/IAB display sizes. PROMOTION PATH: curated AI-generated layouts can graduate to a new BrandCanvasVariant model that lives in templateRegistry alongside hand-authored ones. QUALITY GATE OPTIONS: strict+iterate (judge pass + revise round, higher cost better results) OR loose+curate (operator picks the good ones, save to template library — start here). Replaces the existing aiLayoutStudioService gpt-image-1 path entirely once Phase 1 is proven.

Summary: Cartesian enumeration cap for alt-expanded runs
Description: Once seedsFromProduct emits a product_image seed per (hero + alts), a single product with 4 alts × 3 templates × 3 ratios × 2 paletteSources = 72 product_image ads BEFORE UGC seeds fan in. Existing MAX_ADS_PER_GENERATION_RUN cap (env, default 200) clips total run but the readinessScore desc sort dictates which ads survive — alts may drown out UGC variants. Need a smarter prioritization: per-seed cap (e.g. at most 1 catalog hero + 2 best-scored alts per product), or tier-weighted budget (UGC gets at least X% of slots), or operator-tunable per-product alt budget. Reference: services/campaignAdsGenerationService.js seedsFromProduct + EXPANSION_PRODUCTS_PER_POST pattern. Depends on the seedsFromProduct alt expansion landing first.

Summary: Worker render-loop concurrency
Description: Render service today processes Ad docs one at a time — a 12-ad cold batch (post schema-version bump) clocks ~12-18 minutes wall time because each cell does LayoutInput derive + canvas spec (N=3 + Judge) + HTML gen (N=2 + validation) + Puppeteer screenshot sequentially. Adding 3-4 parallel Puppeteer pages in the worker loop should give a 2-4× speedup proportional to concurrency. Concurrency cap should be env-driven (RENDER_WORKER_CONCURRENCY) so it can be tuned per-deploy; need to verify Render starter tier memory headroom (each Puppeteer ~150-200MB resident). Per-cell LLM round-trips already share OpenAI's per-key rate limits so concurrency there is OpenAI-side, not ours. Photoreal/image-ref is already setImmediate so it doesn't gate the loop.

Summary: Platform-format-aware ad generation (Phase 1a)
Description: Make the Creative Director and HTML Layout Generator format-aware so ads get designed FOR a specific Meta surface instead of generic 1:1 canvases. Phase 1a scope = TWO formats only: meta_feed_1_1 (current default; image+video; no safe areas) and meta_reels_9_16 (vertical; video preferred; safe_top 0-220px + safe_bottom 1558-1778px). Together these prove (a) format flows through both LLM prompts, (b) safe areas can be enforced at the validator, (c) the cartesian partitions cleanly per format. Once shipped, adding meta_feed_4_5 + meta_feed_1_91_1 (Phase 1b) and meta_stories_9_16 (Phase 1c) is config not architecture. DELIVERABLES: 1) Campaign.platformFormat:String field, default 'meta_feed_1_1'. 2) Wizard Step 1 drop-down with the two format options. 3) Pipeline plumbing — campaign.platformFormat → expandWizardJob → Ad.platformFormat → LayoutInputArtifact → Director + Generator inputs. 4) Director prompt new FORMAT CONSTRAINTS section + archetype weighting (Reels deprioritizes TYPOGRAPHIC_DOMINANT, MAGAZINE_EDITORIAL; favors HERO_QUOTE_OVERLAY, FULL_BLEED). 5) HTML Generator prompt new FORMAT CONSTRAINTS section with safe-area pixel boxes (no zones intruding the reserved bands). 6) htmlValidationService new HARD violation safe_area_violation — bounds-check zones against format's safe areas. 7) platformFormat becomes the 9th cache-key dimension on AiCanvasArtifact (same-media+same-product designs for feed vs reels are distinct artifacts). LLM PICKS RATIO — when a format ships multiple ratios (Phase 1b), the LLM picks one per concept rather than forcing cartesian fanout (3× LLM cost saved, designer-quality decisions). Phase 1b adds Director recommended_ratio field + ratio-rotation directive across concepts. OPEN QUESTIONS to resolve before coding: (Q1) Format picker on Step 1 (campaign type) vs Step 3 (settings) — leaning Step 1 since format determines media-seed eligibility. (Q2) Default meta_feed_1_1 = no format-aware prompting (backward compat) OR every campaign goes format-aware with default just meaning 'no extra constraints' — leaning the latter. (Q3) When operator picks Reels but source media is image-only — refuse, warn, or silently drop those seeds from expansion — leaning silent drop via seedsFromProduct filter. DEFERRED — copy-length validation (soft warning only; LLM rarely overshoots), video duration enforcement (LLM doesn't pick duration today), carousels (separate cards[] output schema rewrite), collection (special schema), Audience Network sizes (niche). Approx 3-4 hours backend + 30 min wizard. SEQUENCE: ships AFTER the Veo 3 video-reference integration (row 135) — Veo-generated visual bases need to be the source the format-aware Director and Generator reason about, so the base-video architecture should settle first. Q1 obsolete (Settings step deleted in commit 52cf33c); format picker will land on Step 1 or Step 2.

Summary: ClickUp import script (mirror of import-to-jira)
Description: Backlog parallel of scripts/import-to-jira.js targeting ClickUp's REST API. Auth via personal API token (env CLICKUP_API_TOKEN). Reads docs/backlog.csv and POSTs each row as a ClickUp task. Field mapping: Summary→name, Description→description (markdown), Priority→priority (1=urgent, 2=high, 3=normal, 4=low), Component+Labels→tags (split on ; and prefix component:/label:), Issue Type→custom field OR task_type (Story/Epic/Task), Epic Name→parent task (lookup-or-create), Epic Link→parent task by Epic Name. Auto-skip rows whose name already exists in the target list (incremental import — re-running doesn't dup). Pre-reqs: CLICKUP_LIST_ID env var pointing at the destination list; or wizard flow that creates the list under a configured space if not present. Open questions: (1) Issue Type as ClickUp task type vs custom field — task type is platform-native but requires upfront task-type setup; custom field is portable and matches Jira's notion better. (2) Whether to mirror only High priority rows or the whole backlog. (3) Whether to add a one-way sync (CSV → ClickUp on every push) or keep it manual via npm script. Reuse pattern from scripts/import-to-jira.js for CSV parsing + axios POST loop. Approx 1-2 hours.

Summary: Creative Director: enforce element variety + force per-concept role minimums
Description: Rendered ads cluster on headline + CTA + eyebrow + logo + hero ~90% of the time even when LayoutInputArtifact carries badges, short benefits, brand descriptions, top comments, creator handles, copy_candidates with 5+ quotes. ROOT CAUSE — it's the Director's prompt, not a data-flow bug. All signals reach the Director correctly; the prompt at aiCreativeDirectorService.js buildPrompt() biases toward minimum-surface concepts when proof signals are weak. Specifically: (1) productSignal.badges is NEVER mentioned in the prompt rules — the LLM sees badges in input data but is never told 'if badges.length>=2 you SHOULD surface a badge_row zone.' (2) brand_signal.description / brand_reviews_summary / product_signal.description / product_signal.review_summary are called out only for emotional_hook calibration, never as candidates to surface as visible body copy / text zones. (3) Variety enforcement is too thin — rule says concepts must differ on archetype OR emotional_hook OR social_proof_type (three axes). When HONESTY RULE forces social_proof_type='none' on all four, that axis collapses and the four concepts cluster on archetype+hook variations of the same minimal idea. No requirement that 'concept 2 must surface badges, concept 3 must surface a product detail, concept 4 must surface creator handle.' (4) recommended_components fills are explicitly OPTIONAL (line 428: 'you don't have to fill every role — only the ones the strategy calls for'). Combined with priorities being mostly 'absent', this becomes 'fill almost no roles.' FIXES (land in aiCreativeDirectorService.js buildPrompt() only — no schema or downstream changes): (A) Add badge_row rule — 'if product_signal.badges.length>=2, at least one concept MUST set recommended_components.badges and include badges as a featured element.' (C) Force per-concept role minimums — each concept's recommended_components must specify a style for >=5 roles (headline, cta, logo, plus 2 of: badges, eyebrow, product_card, quote, creator, stat, body_text). (D) Spread variety across concepts — the four concepts as a SET must collectively touch >=6 distinct roles, not just 4 variations on the same 3 roles. DEFERRED: (B) 'when proof weak, surface brand_signal.description as a text body zone' — more philosophical (could produce visual noise); test separately after A+C+D land. Bump DIRECTOR_SIGNALS_VERSION to invalidate cached artifacts. Approx 1-2 hours, all prompt work in one file.

Summary: Copy derivation: fall back to brand-review quotes when product reviews are thin
Description: Symmetric to the Director projection fix (commit 04afb02) but one layer downstream. The LayoutInputArtifact's copy_candidates.quotes is built by services/copyDerivationService and currently only pulls from product-level reviews (product.reviews / product.productReviews). For brand-mode runs (no product) the array stays empty unless something else fills it; for product-mode runs whose SKU has thin reviews, brand-level review quotes (Brand.brandReviews.quotes scraped from WeddingWire / Trustpilot / Google / gemini-search) never make it into copy_candidates. ROOT CAUSE confirmed via inspectLayoutGenInput on a Camelbackflowers brand-mode ad: LayoutInputArtifact.social_proof.primary_quote.text = 'Laura was kind, attentive and so creative!' (from brand reviews) AND LayoutInputArtifact.social_proof.secondary_quotes also pulls brand quotes, BUT copy_candidates.quotes contains five DIFFERENT quotes (Mallory, K. Kelly, Alexia, Mackenzie, Bianca) that come from copy derivation's own brand_reviews_summary parse. The Director sees Laura's quote via assembleSignals + brand-review fallback, correctly picks social_proof_type='testimonial', the JSON Gen materializes a quote_card zone with slot:'social_proof.primary_quote' — but the HTML LLM picks quote TEXT from copy_candidates.quotes (it hardcodes the picked text inline in the HTML, not slot-resolved), so Laura's quote never renders. The HTML LLM picked Mallory's quote instead. FIX: copyDerivationService should include brand-review quotes in copy_candidates.quotes when product-review quotes are thin (or always — they're additive proof). Mirrors aiCreativeDirectorService's brand-review fallback pattern from 04afb02. Surface scope (product / brand) so the LLM can attribute correctly. INVESTIGATION before coding: confirm where copy_candidates.quotes is assembled (likely copyDerivationService.js or layoutInputService.js), confirm the brand-review path isn't already there for some other reason, decide whether to merge brand quotes with product quotes vs surface as separate field for distinct treatment. Approx 1-2 hours.

Summary: LayoutInputArtifact: triage pre-derived input.copy fields (legacy path)
Description: inspectLayoutGenInput on a brand-mode ad surfaced that LayoutInputArtifact.input.copy contains pre-derived strings — headline_lead='Your Vision,', headline_main='In Bloom', headline='Your Vision, In Bloom', subheadline='ARTISTRY &', eyebrow='Event Floral Design' — that DON'T appear in copy_candidates and are NOT visible to the JSON Gen or HTML Gen LLMs. The LLMs work off copy_candidates arrays + index picks (copy_picks.headline_pick etc.). These pre-derived input.copy fields appear to be vestigial from a legacy code path. INVESTIGATE: (1) Where are these fields populated — likely layoutInputService.js or a separate copy-resolution step. (2) Does any code path read them — old V1 templates? Direct slot resolution somewhere? (3) Are they REDUNDANT (just the same strings as copy_candidates picks resolved early) or PARALLEL (different copy that the LLM never sees)? Output for Camelbackflowers showed them as totally different strings from copy_candidates, suggesting parallel. RESOLUTION OPTIONS: (a) Delete the fields entirely if unused. (b) Promote them into copy_candidates as additional options if they're worth surfacing. (c) Keep them for the V1 / legacy path only and document the boundary. Either way the LayoutInputArtifact field should be tagged with provenance so future audits don't keep flagging it. Low-priority cleanup but blocks confidence in future copy-projection audits.

Summary: Veo 3 video-reference polish for video ads
Description: Replace the source IG / Cloudinary video with a Veo 3 image-to-video generation as the base layer in the existing composite chain. Puppeteer chrome (panels / text / CTAs / logos) stays the top layer — Veo only touches the visual base, so brand text remains pixel-sharp. Mirrors the image-ref / photoreal shadow pattern (aiImageReferenceService) but for video. ARCHITECTURE: Cloudinary source video URL → so_0 first-frame still at canvas aspect → Veo 3 image-to-video (5s, canvas aspect) → Cloudinary upload of Veo output → existing videoCompositeService chain (c_crop smart-crop → c_lpad → l_<overlay PNG> → fl_layer_apply) with Veo's mp4 as the new source. Net result: smoother / more polished visual base, identical chrome treatment. DELIVERABLES: 1) services/veoApiClient.js — Vertex AI auth + predictLongRunning + polling for completion. 2) services/aiVideoReferenceService.js — prompt assembly (already prototyped in scripts/buildVeoPayload.js), so_0 first-frame extraction, Veo call, Cloudinary upload, AiVideoReferenceArtifact persist, composite chain rebuild with new base. 3) models/AiVideoReferenceArtifact.js — cache key (mediaId, directionConceptId) so multiple ads from same (media × concept) share one Veo call (collapses 20 ads → ~4 actual Veo calls per typical run). 4) Ad.videoRefUrl field. 5) routes/ads.js exposes videoRefUrl in API response. 6) renderService.js triggers video-ref shadow as setImmediate post-persist when AI_VIDEO_REF_ENABLED=true AND ad.kind === 'video' (mirrors aiOverlayPolishService trigger). 7) Frontend Ads/index.tsx displayUrl() prefers videoRefUrl over renderUrl for video ads, isAwaitingPolish covers video-ref pending. CREDENTIALS: Vertex AI service account JSON, GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS=/etc/secrets/gcp.json (Render Secret File). Single VEO_PROJECT_ID + VEO_LOCATION env block. COST GUARD: AI_VIDEO_REF_MAX_PER_RUN env cap (default 10) so a Generate Ads click can't burn more than ~$25 at $2.50/clip without operator approval. The (mediaId, directionConceptId) cache amortizes across the 5-template fanout. PROMPT STRATEGY: already in scripts/buildVeoPayload.js — concept-grounded (archetype, emotional_hook, brand voice, product, primary subject) with a hard 'DO NOT render any text/logos/chrome' instruction so Veo keeps the frame visually clean for the Puppeteer chrome composite. SHIP STRATEGY: behind AI_VIDEO_REF_ENABLED=false flag so the infrastructure can merge without burning Veo calls until credentials + budget are approved. MANUAL VALIDATION FIRST: run scripts/buildVeoPayload.js on a recent video ad, paste prompt + first-frame still into Google AI Studio Veo 3, inspect output for text fidelity / motion quality / brand-faithfulness BEFORE flipping the flag. If output looks bad, kill the path — script is the cancel point. TRADE-OFFS: cost real (~$50/run uncapped; ~$10/run with concept caching), 30-60s background latency per call (existing poll-extension fix handles UI), 5s output length (suitable for short-form, may want 8s once Veo opens longer durations). Estimated ~4-6 hours backend + 30 min frontend. SEQUENCE: ships BEFORE the platform-format-aware ad generation work (row 130) — Veo-generated visual bases need to flow through the format constraints, and the format-aware Director / Generator prompts will reason more cleanly when the base-video architecture is already settled.

Summary: Opportunity Score engine (Phase 2 — Product Ads + Campaigns)
Description: Drives the 'Good Opportunities' KPI tile + per-row Opportunity Score column on both /product-ads and /campaigns. Today both pages ship the field as null and the KPI as '—'. The engine ranks products / campaigns by likely ad-performance lift = signal × inverse-coverage: high fresh UGC count × high engagement signal × inverse ad coverage × content recency. PER-PRODUCT formula (suggestion): score = clip(0.4*ugc_match_count_30d + 0.3*avg_engagement_rate_30d + 0.2*new_comments_30d + 0.1*new_reviews_30d, 0, 1) × inverse_coverage_factor where inverse_coverage_factor = 1 - min(coveragePct/100, 0.95). PER-CAMPAIGN aggregates the per-product scores across the campaign's matchedProductIds + adds campaign-level signals (recent insights deltas if integration insights endpoint is connected, days since last sync). DELIVERABLES: 1) services/opportunityScoreService.js — pure-function score computation, no DB writes (computed at read-time on /api/catalog/ads-summary + /api/campaigns/ads-summary). 2) Field projection on both endpoints. 3) Frontend table column rendering as circular gauge with color band (red <40 / amber 40-70 / green 70+). 4) 'Generate Ads' dropdown options on both pages — 'Generate for new opportunities' / 'Generate for low coverage' / 'Generate for products with no ads' use the score buckets to pre-filter the bulk-select target. Cost: pure computed, no LLM/SerpAPI spend. Time: ~3-4 hours. Phase 2.

Summary: Automation rules engine (Phase 3 — Product Ads + Campaigns)
Description: Both /product-ads and /campaigns pages have an 'Automation' button in the header that's currently a placeholder. Phase 3 ships a rule engine: operator defines triggers + actions in a JSON-backed schema; a cron-driven worker evaluates rules against the brand's catalog + campaign state and auto-fires Generate Ads runs when conditions are met. EXAMPLE RULES: 'auto-generate 1 Reels ad per product when (UGC matches_24h >= 3) AND (ad_coverage < 50%) AND (opportunityScore >= 70)'; 'when a campaign drops below 60% coverage, regenerate the top-3 low-performing ads'; 'when a new product is detect-identified and promoted to catalog, auto-queue the 5 default templates'. DELIVERABLES: 1) models/AutomationRule.js — Mongoose schema with { brandId, name, enabled, trigger:{ event, conditions[] }, action:{ type, params }, lastRunAt, runHistory[] }. 2) services/automationRuleService.js — rule evaluator + action executor (Generate Ads dispatch, Regenerate dispatch, Notify operator). 3) Cron worker (RUN_WORKER=true existing process) ticks every 15 min, fetches active rules, evaluates triggers, fires actions. 4) routes/automation.js — CRUD endpoints. 5) Frontend Automation modal — rule builder UI with trigger picker (event type + condition rows) + action picker. 6) 'Run automation rule' dropdown option on Generate Ads (one-shot rule run, doesn't wait for cron). Dependency: Opportunity Score engine for most useful triggers. Cost: cron compute only; LLM spend depends on operator-configured rules (need a daily cap per rule). Time: ~6-8 hours. Phase 3.

Summary: Variant tree for ad regeneration
Description: Today Regenerate (POST /api/ads/:id/regenerate) OVERWRITES the existing renderUrl in place — operator can't roll back if the new version is worse. The regenerationHistory[] field stores past PROMPTS so they can be re-entered, but the actual prior render URLs are gone. ENHANCEMENT: keep the original Ad row, create a new Ad row linked via Ad.parentAdId pointing to the original. Both surface in the expansion grid (variant strip showing 'v1 / v2 / v3' tabs). Operator can 'Promote variant' to make a different version the canonical one (swaps parent/child pointer). DELIVERABLES: 1) Ad schema gains parentAdId + variantIndex + isCanonical. 2) adRegenerateService regen path creates a new Ad via Ad.create (not Ad.updateOne) and links to parent. 3) routes/catalog ads-detail projection groups variants under their canonical parent. 4) AdDetailModal gains a variant strip + 'Promote this variant' button. Cost: storage doubles for actively-regenerated ads (cheap). Time: ~3-4 hours. Sequence: ships after operators ask for rollback — currently a known gap.

Summary: Subject motion-aware bbox tracking for video chrome
Description: aiReelsChromeService now passes Media.subjects[] bboxes to GPT as a HARD 'don't overlay the subject' guardrail. For video, the bbox is the seed media's FIRST FRAME — across the 5-8s clip the subject moves and the static bbox becomes stale at later timestamps. The 8 reference frames help GPT visually track but motion-aware bbox data (per-frame subject coords) would be more enforceable. OPTIONS: (1) Run YOLO + subject classifier on each of the 8 sampled frames at Veo-output time; pass per-second bboxes to GPT. (2) Use Cloudinary's saliency / g_auto crop hints across frames. (3) Skip for now and trust the static bbox + visual frames. DELIVERABLES (option 1): after Veo upload, derive 8 still frames via so_0..so_7, send each through YOLO microservice + identify, persist per-frame bbox array on Ad. Pass to chrome prompt as 'subject travels: t=0 at x:200,y:400 → t=2 at x:300,y:400 → ...' so GPT routes chrome to the union complement. Cost: ~$0.05 per ad in YOLO calls. Time: ~3 hours. Phase 2.5.

Summary: TikTok platform format support
Description: Channels on the Campaigns page mockup show 'Meta, Instagram, TikTok' but the codebase currently only supports meta_feed_1_1 / meta_feed_4_5 / meta_reels_9_16 / meta_stories_9_16 / pmax_16_9. TikTok video ads have distinct surface conventions (full-screen 9:16, sound-on, native-creator energy, no native UI overlay over the canvas during in-feed playback). DELIVERABLES: 1) Add tiktok_9_16 entry to services/platformFormats.js with surface='tiktok', kinds=['video'] (TikTok image ads are rare), creativeBrief for TikTok-native tone, chromeStyleHints prioritizing tiktok + ig_reels. 2) Add to Campaign.platformFormat + Ad.platformFormat enums. 3) Wizard PlatformFormatPicker includes a TikTok card. 4) Confirm Veo accepts 9:16 (already does). 5) Existing chrome canvas at 1000×1778 applies. 6) Add 'TikTok' to channel-derivation logic in /api/campaigns/ads-summary. Cost: zero — reuses existing video pipeline. Time: ~1-2 hours.

Summary: Inpainting text from burned-text video seeds
Description: seededUniverseService.rankUgcMedias deprioritizes media with burned-in text (Media.text non-empty) for video runs because Veo bakes overlay text into the generated video. When the brand has ONLY text-burned UGC available, we fall back to one anyway and the Veo prompt tells the model to 'ignore visible text' — but Veo usually can't comply. IMPROVEMENT: before sending the seed to Veo, run an inpainting pass that removes the burned-in text using OCR bboxes + a vision model (Gemini Imagen / OpenAI image edit). DELIVERABLES: 1) services/seedInpaintService.js — takes (seedUrl, Media.text bboxes) and emits a clean PNG. 2) aiVideoReferenceService calls it before fetchAsImage when seedHasText=true. 3) Falls back gracefully if inpaint fails. Cost: ~$0.05-0.15 per text-burned seed (Imagen edit pricing). Time: ~3-4 hours. Phase 2.5 — defer until operators complain about Reels with weird OCR-text bleed.

Summary: Cache the quote-pool selection across templates for a single (media, brand)
Description: layoutInputService.assembleInput runs the 4-tier quote pool (product > category > brand > LLM > synth) inside every LayoutInputArtifact derivation. For a batch of image ads on one product+media, 3 templates fire 3 separate Gemini derivations, each rebuilding the identical quote pool and picking the identical winner. Wasted work: ~11s Gemini per template x 3 templates = ~33s and ~$0.05 per campaign per product. Log confirms same 'product=0 category=0 brand=5 llm=3 -> winner=brand' three times on identical media. DELIVERABLES: 1) Extract quote-pool selection to a small helper keyed on (mediaId, brandId, categoryRef). 2) Cache the winner + secondary list in a Mongo doc or in-process TTL cache. 3) LayoutInputArtifact derivation reads from that cache instead of re-computing. 4) Emit the tier-count log ONCE per (mediaId, brand) instead of per template. Cost: -$0.05/campaign, -33s latency.

Summary: Surface the actual reason for html-gen proof_strategy_unsupported violations
Description: In the last campaign run, 2 of 3 image ads had ALL html-gen candidates flagged with proof_strategy_unsupported and were rendered anyway because AI_LAYOUT_DIRECT_HTML=true bypasses hard blocks. The violation reason is a bare enum string — no info on which proof strategy the Director picked vs which strategies html-gen supports for that template + aspect. Operators can't diagnose whether the concept picked stat_led_social_proof but template only supports quote_card, or something else. DELIVERABLES: 1) Log the offending concept.social_proof_type + the templateSupportedProofTypes list at pre-judge time. 2) Bubble the specific violation into htmlGen[...] result so the render pipeline can distinguish specific proof-strategy mismatches from other issues. 3) Feed template proof-strategy support into the html-gen prompt so the LLM stops picking incompatible strategies. Cost: near zero. Time: ~1 hour.

Summary: Investigate barebones HTML output on ai_social_proof_led (487-char body inner)
Description: Recent Pelagic campaign run: ai_social_proof_led/4:5 rendered with html_len=2836, body innerLen=487 — half the size of the other two templates (ai_brand_led=4117, ai_editorial=4428). Combined with winner_hard_violations=1 (proof_strategy_unsupported), suggests the html-gen LLM couldn't materialize concept.testimonial-realism at 4:5 and shipped a minimal skeleton. The winning brand-tier quote may not actually render in this ad. DELIVERABLES: 1) Fetch the exact rendered HTML for artifact 6a4caa9d7b13860ec3a2e8e1 and inspect what got rendered. 2) Determine whether ai_social_proof_led needs a proof-strategy fallback (e.g. quote_card if stat_led is unsupported at 4:5). 3) Add a min-body-length floor (e.g. 800 chars) to the pre-judge check so extreme barebones outputs are rejected even in direct-HTML mode. Cost: ~$0.15 per rejected candidate.

Summary: html-gen underuses Director's media_picks (imgs=1 on non-grid layouts)
Description: In the recent Pelagic run, ai_brand_led and ai_social_proof_led rendered with body imgs=1 despite the Director providing 2 media_picks per concept (and 2 URLs in the ALLOWED URLS prompt block). Only ai_editorial (a static_grid layout) used all 3 permitted images. Loss of media variety across the batch — the Director specifically curated multi-image compositions and the Generator is ignoring the secondary picks. DELIVERABLES: 1) Strengthen the html-gen system prompt to REQUIRE use of every URL in ALLOWED URLS unless output_shape='single_hero'. 2) Post-render check: count tags in body vs allowed_urls length; if concept.output_shape is collage/grid/multi and imgs < tile_count, flag as a warning. 3) Surface imgs=N/expected in the render log so operators can spot underuse. Cost: near zero.

Summary: Retire dead AiCanvasArtifact minimal-shell rows
Description: AI_LAYOUT_DIRECT_HTML=true retired the JSON canvas-spec Generator, but aiCanvasSpecService still writes minimal-shell AiCanvasArtifact rows for every image ad ('JSON Gen RETIRED — minimal artifact' log line). Nothing downstream reads canvasSpec anymore — aiCanvasHtmlGeneratorService loads context from LayoutInputArtifact + CreativeDirectionArtifact directly. Every image ad still creates one dead row. Storage bloat + confusion for future debugging. DELIVERABLES: 1) Stop writing minimal-shell rows in getOrGenerate when direct-HTML flag is on OR outputKind==='html'. 2) Migration script: drop AiCanvasArtifact rows whose canvasSpec is null AND outputHtml is null. 3) Longer-term: consider moving the html-gen output to a dedicated AiHtmlArtifact model and deprecating AiCanvasArtifact entirely.

Summary: Account for or gate the shadow image-ref generation cost ($0.45+/campaign)
Description: aiImageReferenceService runs gpt-image-2 quality=high asynchronously after every image ad, seeded from the freshly rendered HTML PNG. ~150s per generation, ~$0.10-0.20 per image, ~3 image ads per product per campaign = $0.30-$0.60 in unattributed background cost per campaign. Output persisted as 'image-ref shadow GENERATED' but no user-facing surface consumes it. DELIVERABLES: 1) Confirm what downstream consumer needs the shadow — if none, put the service behind an env flag (AI_IMAGE_REF_SHADOW=false default OFF). 2) If needed, add cost tracking via trackLlmCall so the operator sees spend in the campaign-run summary. 3) Consider dropping to quality=medium (~50% cheaper) if the images aren't quality-sensitive.

Summary: Spread review quotes across concepts within a batch (avoid quote repeat)
Description: In a single campaign run for one product, 3 image ads + 1 video ad all share the same primary_quote from the tier 3 brand pool ('Yes they are amazing…'). Director's copy_picks vary across concepts (different headlines / eyebrows) but the quote is picked independently by layoutInputService per (media, brand) — so it's identical when the media + brand are shared across ads. Poor variety when ads are shown together. DELIVERABLES: 1) When multiple ads in one campaign share (mediaId, brandId), pick top-N quotes and round-robin through them (Director cell -> quote index). 2) OR extend Director's copy_picks to include a specific quote_id per concept, resolved against the tier pool. Option 2 aligns quote choice with concept archetype (e.g. stat_led_social_proof picks metric-heavy quote; hero_quote_overlay picks most emotive). Cost: near zero (quote pool already computed).

Summary: Fix conceptDriven universe count math (catalog+ugc != universe)
Description: conceptDriven log line reports 'universe=10 (catalog=8 ugc=8)' — 8+8=16, not 10. Either the counts overlap (media that both matched the product catalog AND appeared as UGC in ProductMatchArtifact) or they're double-counted somewhere in reporting. Not a functional bug but confuses debugging of universe composition. DELIVERABLES: 1) Trace count sources in campaignAdsGenerationService.expandWizardJob / seededUniverseService.rankUgcMedias. 2) Either dedup before counting (report actual universe size + how many rows in each bucket, with dedup noted) or add a third 'both' bucket in the log to make the overlap visible.

Summary: Detect pipeline: lazy enrichment races DetectRun.status='completed'
Description: runImagePipeline returns after writing detection/crops/match latestArtifacts, but the extended-crops + overlay-zones chain fires as a fire-and-forget promise via .then(). processDetectRun then marks DetectRun.status='completed' before extended/overlayZones artifacts land. Frontend polling sees 'completed' + reads Media.latestArtifacts.extended or .overlayZones = null. Or a second DetectRun kicks off before the lazy chain finishes and orphans the prior runs artifacts. DELIVERABLES: 1) Await the lazy enrichment barrier before run.save() marks completed, OR 2) Add a separate DetectRun.enrichmentStatus field so consumers can tell 'core done' from 'enrichment done'. Files: pipelines/detect.js:301-316 and :621-637.

Summary: Detect pipeline: stale in-memory Media + concurrent denorm races on matchedProducts
Description: runImagePipeline holds an in-memory Media object from an early findById. Match-chain writes update Media.matchedProducts via updateOne, then the lazy enrichment reads the SAME in-memory copy (now stale) to update overlay zones. If a second DetectRun for the same Media processes concurrently (worker restart + partial-unique-index race), the later runs writes can be silently overwritten by the earlier runs stale in-memory denorm being replayed. Under load this can invert product matching. DELIVERABLES: 1) Add a version token (Media.detectVersion or ETag) that updateMediaLatestArtifacts compares before writing. 2) OR re-fetch Media fresh at each write boundary. 3) Consider a distributed lock per mediaId. Files: pipelines/detect.js:238, 593, 974-975, 1525.

Summary: Detect pipeline: extended-crops failures leave no observable marker
Description: Inside the lazy-enrichment promise chain, if generateExtendedCrops or judgeExtendedCrops throws, the .catch() logs the error but no marker is stamped on DetectRun.flags (unlike YOLO which sets flags.yoloFailed). updateMediaLatestArtifacts is still called with extendedDoc?._id || null so Media.latestArtifacts.extended stays null. Consumers cannot distinguish 'never attempted' from 'attempted but crashed'. DELIVERABLES: 1) Wrap the lazy chain in try/catch that stamps DetectRun.flags.extendedFailed=true + errorStage='extended-crops' on failure. 2) Same for overlay-zones stage. 3) Add scripts/rerunExtendedFailures.js maintenance script. Files: pipelines/detect.js:307-316, 628-637.

Summary: Detect pipeline: DetectRun partial unique index race at worker boot
Description: models/DetectRun.js:78-85 defines a partial unique index. Index build happens during DetectRun.syncIndexes() at worker startup. If two worker processes start simultaneously (deploy rollover), both run syncIndexes() in parallel. Between the drop of the old index and build of the new one, a narrow race window exists where duplicate queued runs can be inserted for the same mediaId. DELIVERABLES: 1) Move syncIndexes to a one-time boot-orchestrator script run BEFORE workers spawn. 2) OR use createIndex + background:true with idempotent handling. 3) OR accept the narrow window as low-risk and document it.

Summary: Detect pipeline: bulkWrite ordered=true on catalog mirror can partial-fail
Description: mirrorMatchesToCatalogProducts (pipelines/detect.js:1073) builds a bulkOps array with interleaved $pull + $push pairs across N catalog products and their variants. With ordered:true, if one $pull succeeds but the following $push fails (stale variant doc validation error), all subsequent operations for other products are aborted. Error is logged but non-fatal. Partial-mirror state persists until the next detect run re-runs the mirror cleanly. DELIVERABLES: 1) Switch to ordered:false. 2) Wrap the whole mirror in a transaction. 3) Add per-op error accounting. File: pipelines/detect.js:1073.

Summary: Detect pipeline: matchedProducts denorm write is not atomic with ProductMatchArtifact writes
Description: The match chain creates one ProductMatchArtifact per detected product, then a separate Media.updateOne writes the LATEST matchedProducts array (line 988). Race window between artifact writes and the denorm write means readers can see stale data or partially-updated data. Especially bad if the UI is polling for a completed run at the same moment. DELIVERABLES: 1) Combine artifact writes + denorm write into a bulkWrite or transaction. 2) OR add a Media.matchedProductsAt timestamp + require readers to check against ProductMatchArtifact.createdAt for consistency. Files: pipelines/detect.js:974-997.

Summary: Detect pipeline: no lazy-enrichment timeout error persistence
Description: If runExtendedAndOverlayChain hangs (Gemini API timeout, Cloudinary upload stall), the .catch() logs the error but does not stamp anything on DetectRun. The run stays status='completed' with no indication that a stage timed out. Operator sees 'completed' but no overlay artifacts + no way to distinguish 'timeout' from 'never attempted'. DELIVERABLES: 1) Wrap the async chain in Promise.race with a stage-level timeout that stamps DetectRun.flags.extendedTimeout=true. 2) Same for overlay-zones. 3) Include timeout stage in run.errorStage. Files: pipelines/detect.js:316, 637.

Summary: Detect pipeline: empty crops on YOLO failure produces silent-degradation output
Description: When YOLO fails, products=[] and the pipeline continues with empty products but non-empty subjects/text. Smart-crops generated from safe envelope, judge runs with 0 products, entire artifact chain completes. identifyYoloDetections never runs, no refinedProducts populated. Match service falls back to scene-level matching. Consumer cannot tell '0 products' means 'legitimately empty image' or 'YOLO crashed'. run.flags.yoloFailed marker exists but downstream consumers (ad generation, ad-readiness scoring) do not check it. DELIVERABLES: 1) adReadinessService should check run.flags.yoloFailed before scoring detect stage as pass. 2) Ad generation should reject Media whose most recent run has yoloFailed=true unless operator explicitly overrides. 3) Add a UI badge on Media library showing 'YOLO failed' state.

Summary: Detect pipeline: video no-hero-frame path does not consistently stamp yoloFailed
Description: runVideoPipeline tries IG thumbnail mirror first then falls back to runYoloVideoChain. When both fail and no hero frame is found (line 401-416), a minimal DetectionArtifact is created with heroReason stamped. But run.flags.yoloFailed is only set inside runYoloVideoChain — the thumbnail-only-failed path never touches flags. Result: inconsistent flagging. DELIVERABLES: 1) Always stamp yoloFailed=true when the video pipeline exits with no hero frame, regardless of which path failed. 2) Add a separate flags.videoHeroSource enum so consumers can tell how the hero was chosen. Files: pipelines/detect.js:401-416.

Summary: Detect pipeline: comment-fetch failure silently degrades brand-safety eval
Description: Match chain fetches Comment rows with .catch(() => []). If the fetch fails (DB timeout, connection pool exhaustion), commentTexts is empty. Match service proceeds; brand-safety eval runs on caption + OCR only. No marker is stamped to indicate comments were unavailable. A brand-safety score without comments looks identical to one that legitimately has no comments. Operator cannot audit whether the score is reliable. DELIVERABLES: 1) Stamp DetectRun.flags.commentsUnavailable=true when the fetch fails. 2) Include commentsExpected vs commentsActual counts in ProductMatchArtifact. 3) Ad-readiness / brand-safety score display should show a warning when the flag is set. Files: pipelines/detect.js:865-869.

Summary: Detect pipeline: catalog alt images use full-weight pipeline (cost concern)
Description: runCatalogProductPipeline treats hero and alt Media identically — both run YOLO + subjects-text + smart-crops. Alts skip judge but do everything else. MAX_ALT_IMAGES=12 caps fan-out at 13 DetectRuns per product. For a 200-product catalog sync that is up to 2600 DetectRuns, each firing a full YOLO + Gemini + smart-crop sequence. Costs scale O(N * (1 + alts)) with heavy Gemini spend. Alts arguably do not need full identify — same product SKU. DELIVERABLES: 1) Add ALTS_LIGHT_MODE=true env flag: alts run YOLO only. Cuts alt-detect cost by ~70%. 2) OR reduce MAX_ALT_IMAGES from 12 to 4 for demo brands. 3) OR skip alt detects entirely for demo brands. Files: pipelines/detect.js:472-640, catalogProductDetectService.js.

Summary: Detect pipeline: maybePostMatchReply parameter shape mismatch
Description: After runProductMatchChain returns, if productMatches is non-null and Media.source='instagram', the code calls maybePostMatchReply({ media, productMatch: productMatches }). The parameter is named productMatch (singular) but productMatches is the full result object with .matches[], .totalMatches, .matchSource. Depending on how instagramCommentService destructures, this could cause wrong comment template rendering or an outright crash inside the fire-and-forget promise (silent). DELIVERABLES: 1) Audit instagramCommentService.maybePostMatchReply signature. 2) Rename the param at the call site or extract .matches[0] explicitly. 3) Add a try/catch that stamps DetectRun.flags.commentReplyFailed on error. Files: pipelines/detect.js:278-281.

Summary: Detect pipeline: latestArtifacts.matches update is fragile-but-currently-safe
Description: updateMediaLatestArtifacts (line 1513-1515) replaces Media.latestArtifacts.matches only when ids.matches is an array AND non-empty; otherwise it keeps the prior array. Current behavior is safe but fragile — a bug causing ids.matches to be passed as null (not undefined) would flip Array.isArray(null) to false and keep existing.matches. Also safe. But 'null-like' non-array (0, false, empty string) would flip the check and clear all prior matches. DELIVERABLES: 1) Add a defensive test suite for updateMediaLatestArtifacts covering null/undefined/empty-string/0/false inputs. 2) Consider explicit sentinel values (LEAVE_UNCHANGED symbol). Low priority — current code is safe; this is preventative. Files: pipelines/detect.js:1513-1515.

Summary: Image-ref polish inherits base-render CTA cutoffs + 9:16 aspect drift
Description: Two related image-ref (photoreal polish via gpt-image-1) issues surfaced while diagnosing the bottom-cutoff bug fixed in af47c81. 1) aiImageReferenceService.js:170-190 uses the Puppeteer HTML render as seed for gpt-image-1 with prompt language 'refine this design'. gpt-image-1 treats the seed as authoritative and reproduces layout — so any CTA/text clipping in the base render propagates into the polish output. Options: add a post-render bounding-box lint that regenerates when text-element bottom < 24px, OR harden the polish prompt to explicitly re-compose CTA placement. 2) sizeForRatio() at aiImageReferenceService.js:37-47 maps 9:16 → 1024x1536 (which is 2:3 = 0.667, not 9:16 = 0.5625). When useImageRefAsProduction=true and the frontend swaps in imageUrl, ads either letterbox or stretch. gpt-image-1 supports only 1024x1024, 1024x1536, 1536x1024 — either post-crop from 1024x1536 to 9:16 in sharp, or accept the wider aspect and pad. Summary: Home-page conversational agent (chat drawer that initiates tasks)
Description: A Claude-powered chat drawer on the app home page that lets operators run tasks by asking in natural language, discover features, and see generated ads / products inline in the conversation. ARCHITECTURE: new backend endpoint POST /api/agent/chat streams SSE from Anthropic (Sonnet/Haiku); each tool_use maps 1:1 to an existing REST route so authorization, tenancy, spend caps, and business logic all stay in place (agent is intent-routing only, not a parallel implementation). CAPABILITY REGISTRY: single JS file server/services/capabilityRegistry.js listing every action as { id, title, describe, tier, scope, when, args, execute, estimateUsd?, plan? }. Consumed both by capabilitiesToTools() (Anthropic tool schemas + system-prompt discovery text) AND applicableCapabilities(scope, contextDoc) (UI menus with disabled-with-reason tooltips) so agent and UI never drift. Preconditions expressed as Mongo-style operators evaluated by a tiny matcher (sift or ~40-line evaluator). RISK TIERS: 0=read-only autonomous (inspect ad, list products, spend today); 1=cheap writes with inline confirm (archive, sync catalog, regenerate with prompt); 2=billable writes with confirm + spend estimate + daily-cap check (generate ads, video renders, reframe); 3=external / hard-to-reverse with explicit confirm (publish to Meta, push to Shopify, delete brand); 4=multi-step workflows the agent proposes as a plan of tier 0-3 steps for user approval (onboard brand from URL, generate lifestyle images for products missing them, full-format campaign fanout). UX: structured tool results (not text) render as <ResourceCard kind imageUrl title subtitle badges[] actions[]> — one component covers ads/products/campaigns/brands. Long-running renders subscribe the chat to the existing /generation-inspector SSE so cards slot in as ads finish, with inline retry on failure. Same card used as 'about to do this' preview on Tier 2/3 confirmations. WORKFLOWS DISCUSSED: (a) list & generate lifestyle images for products missing one — mostly wires to aiImageReferenceService with a new catalogProductLifestyleService writing back to CatalogProduct.lifestyle_image; needs per-brand lifestyle style anchors to avoid generic output; (b) generate product videos for the catalog and ship them to Shopify — video-gen exists (Omni-family-routed post-713c2e5) but pushToShopify.js is legacy single-tenant + no video support, needs a new shopifyProductMediaService using Admin GraphQL productCreateMedia + per-brand IntegrationCredential + CatalogProduct.shopifyMediaIds for idempotency + default-to-draft guardrail; (c) redesign per-brand Remotion video variant — favors option B (agent authors JSON variant against a curated primitives whitelist, stored as per-brand style file, deterministic React renders) over agent-writes-JSX; primitive whitelist becomes the creative ceiling with occasional PR-based additions. TRADEOFFS TO DECIDE BEFORE CODING: (T1) autonomous scope — default to read-only + confirm-on-write, but allow per-user 'trusted operator' mode that auto-executes Tier 2 up to a daily $ cap; (T2) capability registry duplication of server validation — mitigate with a nightly test that dry-runs every capability's when clause against a fixture context and asserts consistency with the endpoint's actual response code; (T3) rich-card explosion — start with one <ResourceCard> primitive that handles all kinds uniformly, add specialized cards only when a resource clearly needs them; (T4) LLM model — Haiku for cost + latency on tier 0/1, promote to Sonnet for tier 2+ planning; (T5) session/context — agent should call getContext() tool for currently-viewed brand/ad/campaign rather than have the UI hand-pack context into every prompt (keeps state fresh). VERTICAL SLICE TO SHIP FIRST: tier 0 + tier 1 only, no cost gating, one Tier 4 workflow ('generate lifestyle images for products missing one') as the wow demo — lowest risk (image gen ~$0.04/unit), proves capability registry + rich card + streaming pattern end-to-end, unblocks the higher-tier workflows as subsequent stories under this epic.

Summary: Production environment: promote-via-branch on Render + Netlify + separate MongoDB
Description: Split the currently trunk-autodeploys-to-live setup into staging + production before the first customer-facing release. CURRENT (2026-08-04): trunk push to master (frontend/liquidretail.git) → Netlify autodeploy; trunk push to main (backend/liquidretail_backend.git) → single Render web service (worker in-process via RUN_WORKER=true); yolo_microservice.git → Render Docker; ONE MongoDB cluster shared. All autodeploys from trunk. No separation between dev and live. PLAN (promote-via-branch, not per-push): (1) Keep master/main as STAGING — trunk push still autodeploys to staging.*.reach-social.io (Netlify + Render). (2) Create production branch on each repo (or use tags v*); Netlify site #2 wired to production, Render web-service #2 wired to production; twin yolo_microservice Render service on production branch. (3) Promotion = merge master → production (or tag + PR); prod deploy fires on that merge. INFRA DUPLICATION: (a) SEPARATE MongoDB Atlas cluster (or DB inside same cluster with distinct user + IP allowlist) — production connection string never reachable from staging code path. (b) SEPARATE Cloudinary folder OR sub-account so staging renders cannot pollute prod media library (env-derived path prefix in cloudinaryService.js). (c) SEPARATE OAuth apps — Meta/Facebook/Instagram, Google Ads, Shopify — with prod callback URLs pointing to prod domain only; staging apps stay in dev-mode. (d) SEPARATE integration keys — AtlasCloud (or at least separate spend caps + attribution), Brandfetch, Apify, YouTube. (e) SEPARATE Slack alert channels (SLACK_ALERT_CHANNEL / _FATAL / _STATUS become prod-<name>) so staging noise never wakes on-call. (f) SEPARATE spendGuard daily caps — prod cap sized for real customer volume, staging cap tiny to bound accidental exploration cost. ENV-VAR SURFACE: Render dashboard keeps env-specific secrets per-service (§4a delete rule applies — a key that differs across envs MUST stay in the dashboard, not defaults.env); config/defaults.env stays the base, dashboard overlays per env; Netlify contexts (production, branch-deploy=staging) allow per-context vars in netlify.toml. PRE-RELEASE-MEMORY EXPIRY: current 'direct-to-trunk, no PRs' rule (feedback_liquidretail_direct_to_trunk_prerelease.md in Claude memory) EXPIRES on flip-day — reintroduce PR-only for the production branch (master itself can still take direct trunk pushes as staging; production accepts merges from master only, via PR). TRADEOFFS: (T1) infra cost roughly doubles — 2× Render dynos + second Netlify site + second MongoDB tier (or shared cluster with two DBs) + second Cloudinary quota. (T2) 'push = live' pre-release velocity dies — every prod change needs staging verification then a merge/tag. (T3) DATA MIGRATION on flip-day — staging DB is currently the source-of-truth; either bless it AS prod on flip-day (rename in dashboard, adjust connection string) OR mongodump/mongorestore into a fresh prod cluster; decide before flip. (T4) OAUTH CALLBACK CHURN — flipping to prod domain requires re-authorizing every existing brand's Meta/Google/Shopify credentials; plan an OAuth migration UX (banner + one-click re-auth) before flip-day or the first prod session is dead-on-arrival for existing brands. (T5) PREVIEW DEPLOYS — Netlify per-PR previews are free and worth turning on for design review; Render per-PR previews are paid and probably NOT worth it — staging exercises most of that need. WHAT TO BUILD: (a) render.yaml per repo with two service definitions (staging + production, distinct env-var refs, distinct branches) OR manual Render service duplication with 'deploy from production branch' setting. (b) netlify.toml context blocks (production = production branch, branch-deploy for master → staging site). (c) MongoDB Atlas prod cluster (or same-cluster prod DB with separate user credentials + IP-allowlist scoped to prod Render service). (d) Cloudinary folder policy (prod uploads → /prod, staging → /staging) enforced in cloudinaryService.js via env-derived prefix. (e) Prod OAuth apps registered with each provider, callback URLs updated, keys stored in prod Render service dashboard only. (f) Documented flip-day runbook — DNS cutover if needed, DB seed/migration, first-brand OAuth walkthrough, rollback plan (Render + Netlify both support 1-click rollback per deploy — exercise once on staging first). (g) Update / replace the pre-release trunk-push memory on flip-day. RUNBOOK OUTPUT: short PROD_DEPLOY.md in server/docs and frontend/app/docs describing the merge-master-to-production ritual, expected verify steps, and how to rollback each side. SUCCESS CRITERIA: (S1) A staging deploy cannot mutate a prod DB row, cannot post to a prod OAuth-linked Meta account, cannot charge the prod AtlasCloud budget, and cannot alert into prod Slack channels — enforced by DIFFERENT credentials, not by convention. (S2) A prod deploy is reproducible from a single git commit on the production branch (rollback = redeploy previous commit, no manual step). (S3) The first customer onboard can happen against prod without touching staging.

Summary: Persistent chat sessions — Phase A: ChatSession model + storage + 3 T0/T1 caps
Description: Ship the backend foundation for a persistent-session chat drawer. TODAY the agent is STATELESS — client holds history and re-sends the full array every turn (with AGENT_MAX_MESSAGES temporarily disabled while the drawer catches up). This phase migrates to server-held sessions. DELIVERABLES: (a) new ChatSession model — { advertiserId, userId, brandContext? { brandId?, campaignId?, adId?, productId? }, messages [{role, content, tool_calls?, tool_call_id?}], startedAt, lastActivityAt, retiredAt, retiredReason? }; unique index on (advertiserId, userId, retiredAt: null) so an active session per user is discoverable in O(1). (b) endpoint changes in routes/agent.js — accept optional sessionId in the request body; when present, load messages from Mongo and merge with any incremental messages the client sent; when absent, auto-lookup the caller's most recent non-retired session, or create one lazily; stamp lastActivityAt on every request. (c) three capabilities: chat.listSessions (T0, scope=advertiser) — enumerate the caller's sessions (up to 50, sorted lastActivityAt desc, with title + preview); chat.getSession (T0, scope=advertiser) — fetch one session's full messages by sessionId, tenant-scoped; chat.startSession (T1, scope=advertiser) — mint a fresh session and retire any active one with reason='new-chat'. (d) session-title derivation — first user message's first ~60 chars as a preview; can be refined later. WATCHOUTS: (W1) tenant scope on EVERY session query — cross-user leaks would be a full-page disaster. (W2) message array size — bound at ~500 messages per session to prevent runaway Mongo doc bloat; if we hit the cap we auto-retire and start a new one. (W3) tool_calls / tool_call_id must persist verbatim so the LLM sees intact history on resume; any transform would strand orphan tool_calls. See docs/AGENT.md conversation-flow contract. DEPS: none. Ship first — Phases B + C both key on ChatSession.

Summary: Persistent chat sessions — Phase B: agent.diagnoseGaps (T0)
Description: New T0 capability the LLM auto-calls at session start (see Phase C) to surface actionable work for the operator: per brand under the advertiser, report — products without ads (count + sample 10), catalog products with reviews but no ads (count + sample 10), media that lack a strong match (count + sample 10), campaigns whose most recent generation had failed ads (count + list), connected integrations that have not synced in >7 days (list + lastSyncAt), in-flight workflow runs (chat sessions currently mid-preview / mid-execute). Bounded query cost — advertiserId-scoped, covering-projection selects, hard cap of 100 rows per aggregation with truncated:true flags (same pattern as agent.searchAcrossBrands). WATCHOUTS: (W1) 5k-product brands — products-without-ads is a Mongo $lookup that grows with catalog size; add an index on (brandId, adCount denorm field) OR use a per-brand rollup CostLog-style; DO NOT ship a full $lookup on every session start. (W2) Result shape must be structured (arrays of {_id, name, ...}) not free-form prose — the LLM needs to reference specific ids in the recommendation. (W3) Result truncation ceiling matches AGENT_MAX_TOOL_RESULT_BYTES (12KB) — if the diagnosis payload approaches it, drop to counts-only. DEPS: none, but Phase C depends on this.

Summary: Persistent chat sessions — Phase C: first-turn greeting + diagnosis behavior
Description: When a session is brand-new (ChatSession created within the current request OR resumed after retirement), the agent should greet the operator by name and auto-call agent.diagnoseGaps to surface the top 3-5 actionable items. Also: "pick up where they last left off" = read the LAST retired session's final tool_call (or last assistant message) and mention it as a reference ("last session you were working on regenerating failed ads for Allbirds — want to continue?"). DELIVERABLES: (a) routes/agent.js buildSystemPrompt() adds a session.isNew branch (server determines via ChatSession.messages.length === 0 or by looking at retiredAt on the prior session); the branch instructs the LLM: greet with req.user.name (fallback req.user.email), call agent.diagnoseGaps, format the top gaps as a numbered list with agent-invocable next steps. (b) new T0 cap chat.lastSessionSummary (scope=advertiser) — returns the previous session's final resource + last tool call so "pick up where you left off" is grounded, not hallucinated. WATCHOUTS: (W1) system-prompt bloat — the greeting branch is only appended when session.isNew is truthy; do not ship on every turn. (W2) the diagnosis auto-call still passes through tier gating (T0 is autonomous, so no confirmation needed — but the LLM must not chain into T2+ automatically from the greeting; the prompt must say "suggest next steps, do not execute"). (W3) empty-catalog brands — diagnosis returns all-zero counts; system prompt must handle that gracefully ("nothing urgent — what would you like to work on?"). DEPS: Phase A + Phase B.

Summary: Persistent chat sessions — Phase D: session picker sidebar + idle timer (FRONTEND)
Description: Frontend-repo work in Emami-RS-Project/liquidretail (branch master, frontend/app/src/features/chat/). Left sidebar in the chat drawer lists the caller's sessions (from chat.listSessions), highlights the active one, "New chat" button (calls chat.startSession which retires the current session as new-chat), clicking a prior session loads it (chat.getSession → replaces the drawer's local message state with the persisted history). CLIENT-SIDE 3-HOUR IDLE TIMER — reset on every user action; on expiry, call a new chat.retireSession cap (Phase A additive) with reason=idle-timeout. LOGOUT — the /api/auth/logout flow calls chat.retireSession before clearing session cookies. WATCHOUTS: (W1) session cookies vs. chat sessions are distinct concepts — retiring a chat session on logout is a courtesy; even without it, requireAuth on the next login resolves the correct advertiser and the session picker sees the un-retired row. (W2) SSE reconnect — if a chat is mid-stream when a session switch happens, abort the previous EventSource before opening the new one; do not orphan open connections. (W3) offline-first — the drawer already holds messages in a Zustand store; the picker must NOT wipe local state when the operator hasn't yet clicked into a persisted session (a fresh page load creates a new session server-side, but the drawer's own state still wins for the current turn). DEPS: Phases A/B/C shipped on backend first.

Summary: UGC-ads Phase 2: wizard extension (FRONTEND)
Description: Ship the operator-facing wizard for attaching UGC to a target and generating ads. Wizard-centric design per 2026-08-10 session; frontend repo Emami-RS-Project/liquidretail (staging) → Emami-RS-Project/rs-ai-frontend (prod). Six sub-phases: (2a) wizard shell — persistent left-rail with UGC preview, step indicator, back/next/cancel/confirm footer, keyed off ?ugc=<mediaId> query param entry point. (2b) Step 1 UGC picker — media grid filtered to socialPostType='ugc' OR source IN ('instagram','apify-ig') OR has any operator/branding/promotional assignment. Single UGC per invocation for MVP (batch is Phase 7). (2c) Product path — Step 2 catalog multi-select with typeahead + browse, showing existing attachments pre-checked; Step 3 campaigns filtered to kind='product' with matchedProductIds intersection, each row expandable to show constituent products with per-product checkboxes default-checked to UGC-attached set; Step 4 inline quick-create (name+description, kind inferred, products auto-populated); Step 5 preview + confirm with per-campaign ad-count breakdown, cost, wall-time, seed-cascade preview strip [UGC → product hero → alts]. All Steps 2+ persist attachments immediately via POST /api/media/:id/assign (Phase 1 API) — canceling wizard keeps attachments. (2d) Branding path — Step 2 is a confirm checkbox (no picker); Step 3 filtered to Campaign.kind='brand' with voice signal snippet; seed cascade preview [UGC → brand identity signals]. (2e) Promotional path — Step 2 optional product-callouts sub-picker; Step 3 filtered to Campaign.kind='promotional' with end-date/offer metadata; Step 4 create-form gains offer + endDate fields. (2f) Category variant of the product path — Step 2 radio switches picker to category tree; Step 3 filter is Campaign.kind='collection' + JOIN on categoryRef. WATCHOUTS: (W1) Step 2 → 3 back-nav must PRESERVE persisted attachments (they were saved when Step 2 was submitted); back-button-undoes-my-work is a UX trap. (W2) Empty campaign-list state must prominently offer +Create-new-campaign as primary CTA. (W3) Step 3 constituent-product expansion may be heavy for large campaigns — cap displayed products at 50, show "14 more" with an expand-all click. (W4) UGCs already attached in a different mode (attached as product AND now user tries branding) — wizard should allow both attachment types on the same Media, they're not mutually exclusive. DEPS: Phase 1 shipped (2026-08-10, bf1b5c3). Blocks: Phase 3 (seed cascade), Phase 4 (UGC Ads page), everything downstream.

Summary: UGC-ads Phase 5: video-input UGC passthrough (backend)
Description: New short-path for video-input UGCs (fileType='video'). Currently image-to-video Omni submit costs ~$3/master; if the source Media is a UGC video (IG reel, Apify-scraped video post), the base plate IS the UGC video and Omni submit is wasted spend. Deliverable: skip Omni entirely, compose Remotion chrome titling directly over the source video. Cost drops to ~$0/master (Remotion is free). ~15s wall time vs ~2 min. New service ugcVideoPipeline.js; adRegenerateService understands the new path; kill switch UGC_VIDEO_PASSTHROUGH=true (default off until validated). Verifier revert-proofs the passthrough via source-scan of the pipeline dispatcher — must route fileType=video + UGC source to the passthrough branch. WATCHOUTS: (W1) UGC video may not be in Cloudinary yet if it came from Apify — mirror on first pass via uploadUrlToCloudinary, cache the secure_url on the Media row. (W2) Fallback if mirror fails or takes >30s: fall back to Omni submit (with billing warning) or skip the ad? Decide before ship. (W3) Meta surface aspect ratios — 9:16 UGC videos are already the correct aspect for Reels, but Stories (250 safe zone) + feed 1:1 need re-crop; face-anchored basePlateCropService already handles this. DEPS: Phase 2 shipped so operator can attach UGC videos to products; Phase 3 for seed-cascade parity.

Summary: Wire APPAREL_SHOT_TYPE_RANK into seed picker (apparel-safe seed follow-up)
Description: Follow-up to adgen PR e24b182 (apparel category-aware safety hardening). shotTypeRank now exports APPAREL_SHOT_TYPE_RANK + rankByShotType({apparelSafe:true}) but nothing consumes it. Wire seededUniverseService + campaignAdsGenerationService.rankCatalogMediasForHero to call rankByShotType with apparelSafe=isApparelCategory(product.category) && isApparelSafeSeedEnabled(). Summary: Provider fallback on IMAGE_MODERATION_BLOCKED (nano-banana-2/edit)
Description: When gpt-image-2/edit returns IMAGE_MODERATION_BLOCKED, retry once against google/nano-banana-2/edit before terminating. Different provider = different moderation policy — often succeeds on apparel/swimwear catalog images that OpenAI flags as false positive.
