Fallback should be one-shot (no chain) and clearly labeled in the ledger so cost attribution stays honest. Cheaper too — nano-banana is a fraction of gpt-image-2 price.

Summary: Skip Atlas submits during renderer SIGTERM drain (money leak)
Description: MEASURED 2026-08-25 on run_1787677348712_e426912d: adgen-renderer received SIGTERM at 17:05:59 and continued to fire 6 new atlasImage submits during the 25s drain window. Two receipt-holding predictions were paid for but never uploaded (~$0.14) — recovered later by backend bootRecoveryService but that path is unreliable. Fix: set a module-level shuttingDown flag in atlasImageService (and atlasVideoService) that renderer.shutdown() flips before starting drain; check it at the top of editImage/generateImage and throw a specific ADGEN_SHUTDOWN error the caller treats as claim-release, not fail. Bounded impact — pays for itself in ~30 deploys.

Summary: Cross-process quoteSnippet cache (Mongo or Redis)
Description: Current LRU in quoteSnippetService is per-process. Every new renderer/titler instance starts empty; every new-product ad pays a 15-20s Gemini call for extractSnippet. MEASURED 2026-08-25 (Pelagic swimwear): 15960ms cold call per product; on cache hit ~sub-100ms. Cross-process cache (write-through to LayoutInputArtifact.snippet or Redis) would eliminate the tax on the second+ ad for any product. Highest-value scale item — will hurt more as fleet grows to hit 10k static/hr.

Summary: Derives release claim while polling for master (free MAX_INFLIGHT slots)
Description: Derive path currently holds inflight for up to DERIVE_MASTER_WAIT_MS (60s) polling for the sibling master's veoVideoUrl, then requeues. At target 2000 video/hr with ~11 derives/master, this holds ~110 slots doing nothing per active master. Fix: at claim time, if the sibling master hasn't landed, release claim immediately (don't hold inflight) and let the poll loop re-claim once titlingNeeded/veoVideoUrl is set on the master. Existing requeueDeriveForRetry already handles the release write. Frees inflight slots for statics and other work.

Summary: Wire bootRecoveryService on adgen renderer/titler boot
Description: adgen imports bootRecoveryService and titlingResumeService but nothing calls them. CLAUDE.md documents this as unverified. Consequence: SIGKILL'd renderer's receipt-holding claims (Ad.imageGeneration.predictionId or Ad.veoPredictionId) stay stranded until backend picks them up on its next tick — measured 27min stall on 2 statics 2026-08-25. Wire a periodic bootRecoveryService.run() interval from adgen entrypoint or on renderer.run(). Same interval backend uses.

Summary: Move Sharp composites to worker_threads (event-loop parallelism)
Description: MEASURED 2026-08-25 (run_1787677348712_e426912d): 32 concurrent static submits fired ~2-3s apart because Sharp composite work between SCENE_PRESERVE_applied and atlasImage_submitted blocks the Node event loop. Effective per-instance concurrency ~15-20 vs the nominal 32. Move Sharp composites (reference image prep, logomark composite) into worker_threads via piscina or a small pool. Doubles per-instance throughput. Alternative to just adding more renderer instances.

Summary: Try gemini-2.5-flash for overlayZoneService (4x cheaper A/B)
Description: overlayZoneService currently uses gemini-2.5-pro. Flash is ~4x cheaper and ~2-3x faster on the same shape prompts. Zone analysis is spatial reasoning + JSON schema output — not deep semantic work. Set GEMINI_VISION_MODEL=gemini-2.5-flash on backend, kick a real generation, compare vision QC pass rates against a pro baseline over ~50 ads. If quality holds, ship as default. Reduces detect wait latency on cold products AND ongoing cost per product.

Summary: Try CATALOG_DETECT_PRECOMPUTE=true (eager detect at ingest)
Description: catalogProductDetectService currently defers Gemini vision detect to ad-generation time (on-demand). Cold products pay ~120-150s at generate time. Flip CATALOG_DETECT_PRECOMPUTE=true to restore eager detect at Shopify sync time — every generate then hits the cache and returns in ~0.5s. Trade: pay ~$0.04 per product at sync (per media) whether it becomes an ad or not. Only worth it for high-throughput brands where most products WILL generate. Otherwise keep deferred. Owner call.

Summary: Phase 4 — delete adgen renderer's Remotion titling path
Description: Once ADGEN_TITLER_ENABLED has been true in prod for a stable window (2+ weeks?) and titler proven reliable, delete the renderer's in-process Remotion titling code. Removes the rollback safety net for the handoff flag, so this can only ship after that flag is basically permanent. Cleanup includes: shared helpers (startAdHeartbeat, bumpRunCounter, maybeFinalizeRun, settleNonDraftTerminal, notifyRunFinalized) either consolidate into src/services/renderCommonHelpers.js or move fully to titler.js. Also delete REMOTION_CONCURRENCY / REMOTION_QUEUE_CONCURRENCY env from adgen-renderer. Reduces adgen-renderer memory footprint so it can downsize to standard_plus.

Summary: Downsize adgen-renderer instance post-handoff (pro_plus → standard_plus)
Description: Post-handoff the renderer's peak memory is ~1-2 GB (Node heap + LLM JSON + reference buffers), well below 4GB. Currently on pro_plus (8GB) sized for the pre-handoff Remotion path. Downsize to standard_plus (4GB) once next few runs confirm peak RSS < 2.5GB. Saves ~$50/mo per instance × autoscale peak.

Summary: Chrome pool / long-lived Remotion worker in adgen-titler
Description: Currently each Remotion render spawns a fresh child process → Chrome cold start (3-8s) + Node/Remotion bundle init (~5s with pre-bundle) per ad. At 2000 video/hr that is 5-10 CPU-hours per hour of production wasted on process startup. Options: (a) warm Chrome pool per instance (4-6 headless instances reused via Remotion browser handle), (b) long-lived Remotion worker accepting jobs on socket (bigger refactor). Both save 10-25s per titling. Priority rises once QUEUE_CONCURRENCY=4 is validated and titler wall clock still exceeds target.

Summary: Custom autoscale on queue depth for adgen-titler
Description: Render's default autoscale is CPU-based which lags queue backpressure. Titler workload is bursty (12-21 ads per run every few minutes to hours). CPU stays low between bursts, then spikes past 60% target for ~10s before scaling — too late for the first wave. Custom autoscaler: small poller that reads count(Ad WHERE titlingNeeded=true AND claimedByWorker=null), scales via Render API when depth > N. Requires Render API token. Alternative: overprovision min-replicas (min=4-6) so tail is bounded — simpler but pays for idle capacity.

Summary: Cache brand-name resolution per adgen renderer process
Description: Every ad prints '🔗 layoutInput: brand name lookup failed for X — resolved via brandId FK'. For a run of 9-21 ads on the same brand, that is 9-21 identical DB reads + log lines. Small per-ad cost but noisy. Add a per-process Map<brandId, Brand> cache with TTL, or resolve at layoutInputService cache-write time and stamp on the artifact. Cleaner logs + minor perf.

Summary: Batch multiple intent Director LLM calls (fewer paid calls per run)
Description: Currently each ad's buildLayoutInput triggers its own Director LLM call — 3 intents on same product × 3 formats = 9 identical-ish calls. Batch by (product, format): one Director call returns copy for all 3 intents at once. Cuts LLM cost 3x AND reduces cold-start layoutInput derivation wall clock from 40s per ad to 40s for the whole product. Requires prompt refactor + response schema change.

Summary: Fix reference image selection for Pelagic (WHT variants of wrong product)
Description: MEASURED 2026-08-25 on Pelagic Aquatek Yellowtail: video Omni master reference stack pulled refs 1 and 2 from a DIFFERENT color variant of a RELATED product (3015263001-WHT-*.jpg). Result: Omni composited the WRONG fish graphic in generated frames. Root cause: additional-image selection by feedIndex order doesn't verify same-SKU / same-primary-variant. Fix: filter product image selection to only include refs whose CatalogProduct._id matches the ad's productId (or primaryProductId).

Summary: Rotate composited logoCorner across the batch (dynamic per-ad)
Description: In adgen directImageRenderService.js:2636 the reserved corner is HARDCODED to 'bottom-right'. Measured 2026-08-25 on run_1787694870947_6009320f (9 Pelagic swimwear statics, 2 terminal fails / 22% loss): both terminal fails were 'layout_safe_box: composited logo occludes the product/sleeve'. On on-model apparel/swimwear the natural framing puts the model bottom-right; the deterministic Sharp composite then drops the logo across the sleeve. The 2026-08-25 corrective-note fix helps regen recompose the same corner as background, but doesn't fix first-attempt failures. Structural fix: rotate corner across the batch (hash by adId → one of 4 corners) so failures don't cluster; on regen for layout_safe_box occlusion, deterministically swap to top-left. Requires: (a) logoPlacementFor takes corner param (currently returns bottom-right hardcoded at line 1121), (b) safeBoxInDeliveredPx has corner-mirrored variants OR compute-with-corner, (c) product.logoCorner threaded through buildPrompt call sites, (d) verifyLogoSafeBox pinning geometry for all 4 corners.

Summary: Bounded LLM retry on layout-derivation JSON parse failure
Description: Observed 2026-08-25 on run_1787694870947_6009320f at 21:57:56: '⚠️ layout-derivation failed: Unterminated string in JSON at position 1943'. Silent recovery — the ad completed but with fallback layout data (details unclear from log line alone). LayoutInputArtifact derivation calls an LLM (Director?) that occasionally returns truncated JSON. Should retry once with slightly higher token cap. Currently the call is unretried — 1 in ~30-50 runs. Small cost, quality upside.

Summary: Receipt-free stale-claim reaper (Phase 0 follow-up)
Description: bootRecoveryService only handles ads with a spend receipt (veoPredictionId / imageGeneration.predictionId). Ads that got stuck BEFORE Omni submit (during storyboard prep, reference fetch, layout derivation) have no receipt and are invisible to it. Need a separate release-only reaper for status:'rendering' + claimedByWorker != null + updatedAt < now - 15min, which just clears the claim (does not touch spend receipts — bootRecovery owns that). Safe because renderer's heartbeat updates updatedAt every 60s during processing; 15 missed beats is a genuinely dead worker. Same pattern as backend's own reaper but for adgen-owned claims. Follow-up because the receipt-holding case is where the measured 273-min tail was, and that case is now covered by bootRecovery wiring.

Summary: Phase 2 quoteSnippet L2 cache — SHIPPED 2026-08-26

Expected savings: same-review-different-process no longer duplicates 15-30s LLM cost. Doesn't help FIRST instance per (review, brand, product) tuple.

Summary: Video prompt hardening — measured hallucination patterns from Aug 25-26 runs
Description: Investigation-first, NOT a code change yet. Vision QC verdicts across 5 recent Pelagic apparel video runs show a CONSISTENT set of hallucination patterns beyond the 'zoom toward logo' class Nick's #68 already fixes. Concrete examples with ad IDs: (cc081d) 'incorrect chest logo missing the brand wordmark in all frames'; (cc0827) 'severe product and brand identity drift, foreign logos, mangling of the original brand marks'; (cc082f) 'prominent, incorrect logo on the product sleeve'; (cb4fdd from 22:31 run) 'cat-head logo on back right pocket + colorway drift light-grey to dark-charcoal + added two patch pockets'; (cb4fe9) 'invented brand mark on woven label with gibberish text + added patch pockets + aglets not knots'. FIVE distinct classes: (a) invented chest/sleeve logos, (b) added patch pockets / construction details, (c) gibberish text on invented labels, (d) colorway drift, (e) wordmark degradation. Proposed A/B: additive negative-prompt clauses on the Scene 2/3 building code (NOT OMNI_DIRECTIVES which is frozen and pinned), testing 'do NOT add pockets/patches/labels/logos to areas not visible on source' against baseline. Measure per-class failure rate reduction over 50+ paid masters. Cost: $50-100 for the measurement. Owner sign-off needed on the paid A/B.

Summary: Video vision QC regen loop — money-path design
Description: .ISION QC currently 1-shot for video (no regen). Static has 1-regen. Adding a video regen means paying another $1.20 Omni master per fail, but current failure rate is 43-81% on Pelagic. Money math on a 21-ad-video run with 3 masters: if 2/3 masters fail QC (76% failure rate observed), a 1-shot regen at $1.20 each = $2.40 extra, but if regen saves 30% of would-be-failed masters that's 0.6 saved masters × $1.20 = $0.72 recovered value + downstream derives (up to 12 more) worth ~$X in usable content. Break-even hinges on: (a) regen success rate on Omni Pelagic drift class (unknown — measure), (b) marginal cost of $1.20 vs the discarded asset's value, (c) whether corrective note actually helps Omni (unlike static, video prompt is already frozen — corrective note has less room to steer). Design should mirror adVisionQcService.runPostRenderQc: 1-shot regen with corrective note, gated on failure CATEGORY (recoverable classes only — add-a-logo hallucination yes, complete product-identity swap no). Owner sign-off required on the paid A/B.

Summary: Titler autoscale min raise to 4 — reduces cold-start on burst
Description: Currently autoscale min=1 (dashboard). Post-handoff burst arrives to a single titler that autoscales up over 30-60s. Raising min=4 means the burst hits a fully-scaled fleet immediately. Small ongoing cost (3 extra pro_plus instances × ~$50/mo = $150/mo). Trade for faster titler pickup wait. Nick's browser pre-warm reduces per-render cold start; the FLEET cold-start on burst arrival is a separate problem this addresses. Alternative: queue-depth autoscale via Render API (more code effort but no idle cost).
